📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Government of India, Cabinet Secretariat (hereafter Cabinet Secretariat) has released Advertisement No. 02/2026 for direct recruitment to the post of Deputy Field Officer (Technical), also written as DFO Technical. The notification was published in Employment News (17–23 October 2026 issue). Applications are invited from Indian Nationals who hold a valid GATE Score Card. The post is in Level-7 of the Pay Matrix, Group 'B', Non-Gazetted, and the initial posting is at New Delhi. The closing date for receipt of applications is 15 November 2026.

Download Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026 Notification PDF

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026 – Quick Summary

  • Who is recruiting? Government of India, Cabinet Secretariat.
  • Which post? Deputy Field Officer (Technical).
  • How many vacancies? The notification states a total of 250 (tentative). The subject-wise figures printed in the notification add up to 250 (see the vacancy section below).
  • Who can apply? Indian Nationals with a Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology, or a Master's degree in Science, in one of the notified subjects, and a valid GATE Score Card.
  • Application start date: Not specified in the notification.
  • Last date: 15 November 2026 (last date for receipt of applications).
  • Application mode: Offline. The filled-in form must be sent by ordinary post.
  • Job location: The initial posting is at New Delhi. The job involves field postings with All India Transfer liability.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026 Overview

The table below gives the main details of the Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026 as printed in the official notification.

Particular Details
Organization Government of India, Cabinet Secretariat
Advertisement No. 02/2026
Post Name Deputy Field Officer (Technical)
Type of Recruitment Direct recruitment of Indian Nationals with a valid GATE Score
Pay Level Level-7 in Pay Matrix
Post Category Group 'B', Non-Gazetted
Total Vacancies 250 (tentative, as stated in the notification)
Application Mode Offline (by ordinary post)
Closing Date 15 November 2026
Selection Process GATE Score and Interview
Place of Posting New Delhi (initial); field postings with All India Transfer liability

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Important Dates

The notification gives only the closing date. The application start date and the interview date are not specified.

Event Date
Notification published in Employment News 17–23 October 2026 issue
Application start date Not specified in the notification
Last date for receipt of applications 15 November 2026
Interview date, time and centre Not specified. These will be intimated to shortlisted candidates through their e-mails.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Vacancy 2026

The notification lists subject-wise vacancies, which it describes as tentative. Candidates must hold the matching GATE paper in a valid GATE Score Card. The notification states the total as 250, but the subject-wise numbers printed below add up to 250. The notification does not explain this difference, so candidates should confirm the figures in the official notice. The notification also does not give a category-wise (reservation) breakup of vacancies.

S. No. Subject Vacancies Corresponding GATE Paper GATE Code
a Computer Science / Information Technology 112 Computer Science and Information Technology CS
b Electronics and / or Communication / Telecommunication 112 Electronics and Communication Engineering EC
c Data Science / Artificial Intelligence or Computer Science with specialization in Data Science / Artificial Intelligence 10 Data Science and Artificial Intelligence DA
d Physics 05 Physics PH
e Mechanical Engineering 04 Mechanical Engineering ME
f Civil Engineering 03 Civil Engineering CE
g Chemistry 02 Chemistry CY
h Mathematics 01 Mathematics MA
i Statistics 01 Statistics ST

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is checked as on the closing date. Candidates must satisfy the age limit, the educational qualification and the valid GATE Score requirement. They must also clear the character and antecedent verification and the medical examination.

  • Applicant must be an Indian National.
  • Applicant must have qualified in the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) and hold a valid GATE Score Card.
  • A valid GATE Score means the candidate achieved qualifying cut-off marks in GATE 2024, 2025 or 2026 in the notified subjects.
  • A candidate can apply for only one subject out of the notified subject codes.
  • The combination of the educational qualification and the GATE paper must match the subject table above.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Qualification

The Educational Qualification (EQ) for the Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical post is a Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology, or a Master's degree in Science, in one of the subjects mentioned in the vacancy table. The degree must be from a recognised University or Institution. The candidate's GATE paper in the valid GATE Score Card must correspond to the subject applied for.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Age Limit

The age limit is not exceeding 30 years. Age is counted as on the closing date. The upper age limit is relaxable for the identified categories, namely SC, ST, OBC, Central Government Employees and Ex-Servicemen, as per Central Government orders in force. The notification does not give the number of years of relaxation for each category.

Particular Details
Maximum age Not exceeding 30 years
Minimum age Not specified in the notification
Age relaxation Relaxable for SC / ST / OBC / Central Government Employees / Ex-Servicemen as per Central Government orders in force
Age calculated as on Closing date (15 November 2026)

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Application Fee

The application fee is not specified in the notification.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Salary

The post of Deputy Field Officer (Technical) is in Level-7 of the Pay Matrix. According to the notification, the total initial monthly emoluments, including all allowances, will be approximately Rs. 1,00,000 for a posting at New Delhi. The notification does not give the pay-scale range for Level-7.

Particular Details
Pay Level Level-7 in Pay Matrix
Total initial monthly emoluments (including all allowances) Rs. 1,00,000 (approx) in case of posting at New Delhi

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Selection Process

Selection is based on the GATE Score and an Interview. It is subject to the candidate fulfilling the prescribed eligibility criteria, character and antecedent verification, and a medical examination.

  1. All applications received by the closing date that satisfy the eligibility criteria will be arranged in order of merit on the basis of valid GATE Score, for each subject separately.
  2. Candidates will be shortlisted on the basis of valid GATE Score, in a number five times the number of vacancies, and called for Interview.
  3. Final selection is based on GATE Score and Interview.
  4. Selected candidates are subject to character and antecedent verification and a medical examination. The medical standard will be as per the Central Government guidelines applicable to Group 'B' posts.

The notification does not give the marks or weightage for the GATE Score and the Interview.

Documents Required for Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026

Candidates must send the duly filled-in Application Form along with self-attested copies of the following documents.

  • Mark-sheets and certificates (hard copy) of Matriculation, 10+2, B.E. / B.Tech. / M.Sc.
  • Birth Certificate or other relevant documents (Matriculation Certificate, Passport, Driving License, PAN Card) in support of age.
  • Valid GATE Score Card.
  • Caste Certificate (Annexure-I or Annexure-II), for age relaxation, if applicable.
  • NOC from present employer, if applicable.
  • Undertaking (Annexure-III) and discharge certificate, in case of ex-servicemen.
  • Two recent passport size coloured photographs, with name and date of birth on the back.
  • Self-attested copy of the Aadhaar Card (the application form carries the instruction to attach it).

How to Apply for Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Recruitment 2026

The notification describes an offline process. It does not mention an online application link or an official website for applying.

  1. Choose one subject out of the notified subjects and note the corresponding GATE subject code.
  2. Fill in the Application Form, "Application for the post of Deputy Field Officer (Technical) in Cabinet Secretariat (Government of India)", printed with the notification. The form must be typed on A-4 size paper and filled in English capital (block) letters using black or blue ink only.
  3. Do not leave any column blank. Affix a self-attested recent passport size coloured photograph. Sign the declaration with the date and place.
  4. Attach the self-attested copies of all required documents.
  5. Put the application form and documents in an envelope and send it by ordinary post to: Post Bag No. 001, Lodhi Road Head Post Office, New Delhi-110003.
  6. Make sure the application reaches the address on or before 15 November 2026, which is the last date for receipt of applications.

Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Application Form Details

The application form printed in the notification asks for the following information.

  • Subject applied for, subject of B.E. / B.Tech. / M.Sc., and the corresponding subject code in GATE.
  • Name of the candidate, nationality, gender, address for correspondence (state and PIN code clearly), and native place.
  • Mobile number (mandatory) and alternate number; email ID (mandatory, in block letters) and alternate email ID.
  • Aadhaar number, father's name, mother's name, date and place of birth, age as on closing date, and religion.
  • Category (General, SC, ST, OBC, Ex-Serviceman, Central Govt. Employee or Others). A self-attested copy of the requisite certificate must be enclosed when claiming age relaxation.
  • For ex-servicemen, the length of Defence Service (with a self-attested copy of the discharge summary).
  • Marital status and, if married, name, religion and nationality of spouse.
  • Educational qualifications from matriculation onwards (as on closing date): exam / degree passed, board / university, month and year of passing, duration of the course, subjects studied, and total marks obtained in percentage / CGPA.
  • GATE details: year of passing, GATE roll number, subject paper and code, GATE score, GATE marks out of 100, and the date till which the GATE Score Card is valid.
  • Whether employed or not and, if yes, details of employment (department, rank, pay level, date of joining) with a self-attested copy of the NOC from the employer.
  • Declaration that the candidate fulfils the eligibility conditions for the post and has not submitted any other application in response to this selection process.

Important Instructions for Cabinet Secretariat DFO Technical Candidates

  • Applications without a photograph or the requisite certificates / information will not be entertained. Unsigned or incomplete applications will be summarily rejected.
  • Persons in Government service must submit their applications through their respective office and should enclose the Certificate (Annexure-IV) issued by the Competent Authority for claiming age relaxation, if required, as per Government Rules.
  • The job involves field postings with All India Transfer liability.
  • The exact date, time and centre of the interview will be intimated to the shortlisted candidates through their e-mails.
  • The Cabinet Secretariat reserves the right to cancel or withdraw the recruitment process, or revise the number of vacancies, at any stage without assigning any reason.
  • If any information is found incorrect at any stage, the candidature or appointment is liable to be cancelled or terminated without notice, as stated in the declaration.

Annexures Printed with the Notification

The notification includes four formats that candidates may need, depending on their category.

Annexure Format Required From
Annexure-I Format for SC / ST Certificate SC / ST candidates claiming age relaxation
Annexure-II Form of certificate for Other Backward Classes applying for appointment to posts under the Government of India OBC candidates claiming age relaxation
Annexure-III Undertaking to be given by the Ex-Servicemen Ex-servicemen
Annexure-IV Form of certificate to be submitted by Central Government Civilian Employees seeking age-relaxation Central Government civilian employees

Annexure-I notes that ST candidates belonging to Tamil Nadu State should submit the caste certificate only from the Revenue Divisional Officer. Annexure-II states that the OBC certificate must also certify that the candidate does not belong to the persons / sections (Creamy Layer) mentioned in the Government of India Department of Personnel and Training O.M. No. 36012/22/93-Estt (SCT) dated 8.9.1993, as amended from time to time. Annexure-IV is to be filled by the Head of the Office or Department and certifies the pay scale and 3 years of regular service in the grade as on the closing date.

The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India, have released the RRB NTPC Graduate Recruitment 2026 notification under CEN No. 06/2026 for 3,548 vacancies in Non-Technical Popular Categories (Graduate).

The recruitment includes Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, Goods Train Manager, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Senior Clerk cum Typist posts. Eligible graduates can submit the online application from 08 October 2026 to 06 November 2026 at 11:59 PM.

Candidates can check the RRB NTPC Graduate vacancy, salary, qualification, age limit, application fee, selection process, CBT exam pattern, application procedure, signature size and other important details below.

Is Typing Skill Test Required for RRB NTPC Graduate 2026?

No. The Typing Skill Test for Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Senior Clerk cum Typist has been dispensed with for CEN No. 06/2026.

However, candidates appointed to these posts are expected to have basic computer and typing proficiency. Their proficiency may be assessed after joining, and unsatisfactory performance may affect or delay confirmation or promotion.

There is no Typing Skill Test under CEN 06/2026, including for Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Senior Clerk cum Typist.

Candidates will be shortlisted for Document Verification RRB-wise in the ratio of approximately 1:1 against the notified vacancies, based on merit and the applicable recruitment rules.

RRB NTPC Graduate Apply Online 2026

The RRB NTPC Graduate online application process starts on 08 October 2026. Candidates must complete their application by 06 November 2026 at 11:59 PM.

How to Apply for RRB NTPC Graduate Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official RRB application portal.
  2. Open the application for CEN No. 06/2026 – NTPC Graduate.
  3. Select Create an Account if you do not already have an RRB account.
  4. Candidates who created an account for earlier RRB CENs in 2024, 2025 or 2026 should use the same login credentials.
  5. Complete Aadhaar/DigiLocker identity authentication where applicable.
  6. Select only one RRB carefully.
  7. Enter personal, educational, category and other required details.
  8. Choose eligible Railway/Production Unit and post preferences.
  9. Capture the live photograph through the application portal.
  10. Upload the signature in the prescribed format.
  11. Pay the applicable examination fee.
  12. Preview all information carefully.
  13. Submit the application before 06 November 2026 at 11:59 PM.
  14. Save the registration details and submitted application for future reference.

Important: Candidates must submit only one application against CEN No. 06/2026. Multiple applications to the same or different RRBs can lead to rejection of all applications and debarment from future RRB/RRC examinations.

RRB NTPC Application Correction Window 2026

The application modification window will be open from 09 November to 18 November 2026.

Candidates can modify eligible application details by paying a ₹250 non-refundable modification fee for each occasion.

Details entered under Create an Account, including mobile number and email ID, and the Chosen RRB cannot be changed.

RRB NTPC Graduate Photo and Signature Size 2026

For RRB NTPC Graduate CEN 06/2026, candidates are not required to upload a pre-existing passport photograph. The application portal will capture a live photograph during the online application process.

RRB NTPC Live Photo Requirements

  • The photograph must be captured live using a computer/laptop webcam or mobile phone front camera.
  • Use a pure plain white background.
  • Wear non-white clothing, preferably a plain dark colour, to maintain contrast.
  • Look directly at the camera with a neutral expression.
  • The entire face must be clearly visible and centered.
  • The head should occupy at least 50% of the photograph area.
  • Do not wear a cap, mask or spectacles while capturing the photograph.
  • Do not photograph a printed or existing digital photograph.

Important: Since the photograph is captured live, there is no separate RRB NTPC photo upload size or KB requirement for a pre-existing photograph under CEN 06/2026.

RRB NTPC Signature Size 2026

File Format JPG / JPEG
File Size 30 KB to 49 KB
Minimum Dimensions 140 × 60 pixels
Scanner Resolution Minimum 100 DPI
Signature Box 35 mm × 20 mm
Ink Black ink on white paper

The signature must be written by the candidate in normal running handwriting. Signatures written in BLOCK LETTERS, CAPITAL LETTERS or disjointed letters are not accepted.

RRB NTPC Signature Compressor and Image Resizer

If the scanned signature does not meet the RRB NTPC upload requirements, candidates can use the OnlyJobs Image Resizer to resize and compress it before uploading.

For RRB NTPC Graduate CEN 06/2026, keep the signature in JPG/JPEG format, between 30 KB and 49 KB, with minimum dimensions of 140 × 60 pixels.

How to Resize RRB NTPC Signature

  1. Sign on white paper using a black ink pen.
  2. Scan the signature clearly.
  3. Open the OnlyJobs Image Resizer.
  4. Keep the image dimensions at least 140 × 60 pixels.
  5. Compress the file to between 30 KB and 49 KB.
  6. Save the final image in JPG or JPEG format.
  7. Check that the signature is complete, clear and clearly visible before uploading.

RRB NTPC Graduate Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Read CEN No. 06/2026 completely before submitting the application.
  • Applications can be submitted only through online mode.
  • Select only one RRB.
  • Submit only one application against CEN 06/2026.
  • Candidates awaiting their final graduation result are not eligible.
  • Check the medical standard applicable to each post before giving post preference.
  • Goods Train Manager requires A2 medical standard.
  • Capture the live photograph exactly according to the instructions.
  • Upload the signature only in the prescribed format and size.
  • Keep your registered mobile number and email ID active throughout the recruitment process.
  • Details entered in Create an Account and the selected RRB cannot be changed later.
  • Check all details carefully before the application deadline.

Canara Bank Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

All eligibility conditions, including age and qualification, are computed as on 01.09.2026 (inclusive). The tables below summarise the main conditions.

Canara Bank Apprentice Qualification

 
Educational Qualification A Degree (Graduation) in any discipline from a university recognized by the Govt. of India, or any equivalent qualification recognized as such by the Central Government.
Graduation Passing Window Candidates must have passed their Graduation not earlier than 01.01.2023 and not later than 01.09.2026 (both days inclusive).
Test of Local Language Candidates who produce a 10th or 12th standard mark sheet/ certificate showing they studied the opted local language will not have to take the local language test. For other candidates, the test will be conducted when they are called for Document Verification. Candidates who fail to qualify will not be engaged as apprentices.
Physical/ Medical Fitness Engagement is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit as per the requirement of the Bank.
Portal Registration Candidates need a 100% complete profile on https:/ / nats.education.gov.in before applying.

Canara Bank Apprentice Age Limit

The age limit is a minimum of 20 years and a maximum of 28 years as on 01.09.2026. Candidates must have been born not earlier than 02.09.1998 and not later than 01.09.2006 (both days inclusive). The maximum age limit applies to General Category and EWS candidates.

Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

Other Eligibility Conditions and Notes

  1. Age relaxation for SC/ ST/ OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) candidates is allowed on a cumulative basis with only one of the remaining categories for which age relaxation is permitted.
  2. Candidates seeking age relaxation must submit the necessary certificate(s) in original along with photocopies at the time of document verification/ reporting for On-the-Job training and at any later stage required by the Bank.
  3. Reservation for PwBD is horizontal and within the overall training vacancies for the State.
  4. No Ex-servicemen/ Disabled Ex-Servicemen shall be engaged as an apprentice, and there is no reservation for them in this engagement.
  5. The candidate should not have undergone Apprenticeship Training with Canara Bank or any other organization earlier, should not be pursuing Apprenticeship Training under the Apprentices Act 1961, and should not have been terminated during Apprenticeship Training due to their own fault.
  6. Candidates who have undergone training or have job experience of one or more years after completing their educational qualification are not eligible.
  7. SC/ ST/ OBC/ PwBD candidates need a Caste/ Category Certificate issued by a competent authority in the format prescribed by the Government of India.
  8. OBC candidates need a valid OBC certificate with a non-creamy layer clause. OBC candidates who come under the creamy layer are not entitled to OBC reservation and should indicate their category as General in the online application.

Canara Bank Apprentice Reservation Details

Reservation for SC/ ST/ OBC/ EWS/ PwBD candidates is as per the prescribed reservation percentages of the respective States/ UTs as per Government guidelines. Candidates from reserved categories, including those for whom no reservation is mentioned, may apply for unreserved vacancies if they fulfil all eligibility conditions applicable to the unreserved category.

PwBD Reservation

Under section 34 of "The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016", persons with benchmark disabilities are eligible for reservation. The post is identified as suitable for the following disability categories as defined in the Schedule of the RPwD Act 2016.

  • Visual Impairment (VI): Persons with blindness (total absence of sight; visual acuity less than 3/ 60 or less than 10/ 200 (Snellen) in the better eye with best possible correction; or limitation of the field of vision subtending an angle of less than 10 degrees) or low vision (visual acuity not exceeding 6/ 18 or less than 20/ 60 up to 3/ 60 or up to 10/ 200 (Snellen) in the better eye with best possible correction; or limitation of the field of vision subtending an angle of less than 40 degrees up to 10 degrees).
  • Hearing Impaired (HI): Deaf (70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears) or Hard of Hearing (60 DB to 70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears).
  • Orthopedically Challenged/ Locomotor Disability (OC/ LD): Inability to execute distinctive activities associated with movement of self and objects resulting from affliction of the musculoskeletal or nervous system or both, including Cerebral Palsy, Leprosy Cured, Dwarfism (adult height of 4 feet 10 inches (147 centimeters) or less), Muscular Dystrophy, Acid Attack Victims, Spinal Deformity and Spinal Injury without any associated neurological/ limb dysfunction.
  • Intellectual Disability (ID): Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), Specific Learning Disability (SLD) and Mental Illness (MI), as defined in the notification.
  • Multiple Disabilities: Multiple disabilities among the categories above.

Only persons with benchmark disabilities are eligible for reservation. A benchmark disability means not less than 40% of a specified disability, as certified by the certifying authority. Candidates must submit a disability certificate issued by a Competent Authority as per Government of India guidelines, which is subject to verification or re-verification at any point. PwBD reservation is not applicable on the basis of a temporary disability certificate. It is only for persons with irreversible permanent benchmark disability in terms of O.M. No. 36035/ 8/ 2023-Estt. (Res-II) dated 19.05.2023 of DoPT. Government guidelines may change from time to time.

EWS Reservation

  • Persons not covered under the reservation schemes for SC, ST and OBC, and whose family gross annual income is below Rs. 8.00 lakh, are identified as EWS. Income includes all sources (salary, agriculture, business, profession, etc.) for the financial year prior to the year of application.
  • Families owning any of these assets are excluded irrespective of income: 5 acres of agricultural land and above; a residential flat of 1000 sq. ft. and above; a residential plot of 100 sq. yards and above in notified municipalities; a residential plot of 200 sq. yards and above in areas other than notified municipalities.
  • Property held in different locations or cities is clubbed for the land or property holding test.
  • The EWS benefit requires an Income and Asset Certificate issued by a Competent Authority in the format prescribed by the Government of India. Shortlisted candidates must bring it at document verification.
  • "Family" includes the candidate, parents and siblings below 18 years, and the spouse and children below 18 years.

Disclaimer in the notification: EWS vacancies are tentative and subject to further directives of the Government of India and the outcome of any litigation.

Canara Bank Apprentice Stipend and Salary

Apprentices are not employees of Canara Bank. A monthly stipend is paid instead of a salary during the apprenticeship period.

 
Monthly Stipend Rs. 16,650 (including subsidy amount, if any, by Govt. of India)
Paid by Canara Bank Rs. 10,500 per month into the apprentice's account
Government Share Rs. 6,150, credited directly to the apprentice's bank account through DBT mode as per extant guidelines
Deductions Stipend is paid each month after adjusting loss of pay, if any
Other Allowances/ Benefits Not eligible for any other allowances or benefits

Canara Bank Apprentice Application Fee

The fee is non-refundable and includes GST. It is payable online only.

 
Category Application Fee / Intimation Charges (Non-Refundable)
SC/ ST/ PwBD NIL
All Others Rs. 500 (incl. intimation charges)

Payment can be made by Debit Cards (RuPay/ Visa/ MasterCard/ Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, Cash Cards or Mobile Wallets. An e-receipt is generated after a successful transaction. Candidates should not press Back or Refresh after submitting payment information, to avoid double charge.

Canara Bank Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is merit-based. The notification does not describe a written examination.

  1. Merit list: Prepared state-wise in descending order of marks/ percentage in 12th Std (HSC/ 10+2)/ Diploma Examination. Ties are ranked by age in descending order.
  2. Minimum marks: Not less than 60% (55% for SC/ ST/ PwBD) in 12th Std/ Diploma. Fractions are ignored, so 59.99% is treated as below 60% and 54.99% as below 55%.
  3. Document Verification and local language test: Conducted during the Document Verification process. Original documents are checked. Any discrepancy leads to summary disqualification.
  4. Final selection is subject to verification of eligibility and application information, qualification in the local language test of the opted State where applicable, and being declared medically fit.

Where CGPA/ OGPA is awarded, it must be converted into percentage in the online application, with a certificate from the appropriate authority stating the conversion norms. Percentage is total marks obtained in all subjects in all semesters/ years divided by aggregate maximum marks, multiplied by 100. The merit list is prepared only on the information submitted in the online application.

How to Apply for Canara Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates must apply online. No other mode of application will be accepted.

Canara Bank Apprentice Apply Online

  1. Register on https:/ / nats.education.gov.in and complete your profile to 100%. Keep the enrollment number generated.
  2. Visit www.canarabank.bank.in, open Careers, then Recruitment, then the link "Engagement of Graduate Apprentices in Canara Bank under Apprentices Act, 1961 for FY 2026-27".
  3. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic information. A provisional registration number and password are generated and sent by email and SMS. Saved data can be reopened using them.
  4. Enter the NATS enrollment ID, fill all fields, and choose one State along with district preferences.
  5. Upload the photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration as specified below.
  6. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to verify details. No change is possible after clicking FINAL SUBMIT.
  7. Pay the fee online (if applicable), then take a printout of the application and e-receipt.

Apply well before the closing date to avoid website load issues. Only one application should be submitted; if multiple are submitted, only the latest valid completed application is retained.

Documents Required to Apply Online

Upload Specifications
Document Dimensions (preferred) File Size Other Requirements
Photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm) 200 x 230 pixels 20 KB to 50 KB Recent colour passport-style photo on a light background; caps, hats and dark glasses not accepted
Signature 140 x 60 pixels 10 KB to 20 KB Black ink on white paper; CAPITAL LETTERS not accepted
Left thumb impression 240 x 240 pixels at 200 DPI (3cm x 3cm) 20 KB to 50 KB jpg/ jpeg; black or blue ink on white paper
Handwritten declaration 800 x 400 pixels at 200 DPI (10cm x 5cm) 50 KB to 100 KB jpg/ jpeg; English, black ink, own handwriting, not in CAPITAL LETTERS

The declaration text is: "I, ____ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required." Candidates without a left thumb may use the right thumb or other alternatives given in the notification, and must mention the finger and hand/ toe used in the uploaded document. Candidates who cannot write may type the declaration and put their left thumb impression below it. Images should be scanned at a minimum of 200 dpi in true colour, in JPG/ JPEG format. Unclear or smudged images may lead to rejection.

Candidates also need a valid personal email ID and mobile number, active until the process ends, and should spell their name as in the SSC/ SSLC/ X Standard marks card (or as per Gazette Notification/ Marriage Certificate if changed). An application that is incomplete or has unsuccessful fee payment is invalid. If no email/ SMS intimation is received, the application is considered not successfully registered.

Documents to Be Produced at the Time of Engagement

Originals with a self-attested photocopy must be submitted, failing which the candidate may not be permitted to join.

  • Valid system-generated printout of the online application.
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate from a Competent Authority or SSLC/ Std. X Certificate with date of birth).
  • Photo ID: Passport, Aadhar Card, PAN Card, Voter ID, Driving License or any other photo ID issued by Statutory Authorities.
  • Mark sheets/ certificates from SSC onwards to the highest examination passed, including semester/ year-wise mark sheets and the final degree, with proper Board/ University proof that the result was declared on or before the cut-off date.
  • Income and Asset Certificate in the prescribed format (EWS candidates).
  • Caste Certificate in the prescribed format (SC/ ST/ OBC). For OBC, the certificate must include the non-creamy layer clause, be valid as on the date of notification, and the caste name must tally letter by letter with the Government list.
  • UDID card and Disability Certificate from a Medical Board (at least three members, including a specialist) in the prescribed format (PwBD candidates).
  • Any other relevant documents in support of eligibility.

What Are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions. These commissions recruit candidates for various posts and services under state government departments according to the rules applicable to each recruitment.

State PSC recruitment is not limited to State Civil Services examinations. Public Service Commissions may also recruit candidates for engineering, medical, teaching, agriculture, legal, scientific, technical, administrative and other departmental posts.

The posts available depend on vacancies reported by the respective state government departments and the recruitment notifications issued by the commission.

Popular Posts Recruited Through State PSCs

State Public Service Commissions recruit candidates for a wide range of government posts. Common recruitment categories may include:

  • State Civil Services
  • Administrative Services
  • Assistant Commissioner
  • Assistant Director
  • Assistant Professor
  • Lecturer
  • Medical Officer
  • Veterinary Officer
  • Assistant Engineer
  • Assistant Executive Engineer
  • Agriculture Officer
  • Food Safety Officer
  • Drug Inspector
  • Scientific Officer
  • Law Officer
  • Labour Officer
  • Revenue-related Posts
  • Technical Officers
  • Departmental Officers

The actual posts available vary by commission and recruitment notification.

PSC Jobs by Group (Group 1, 2, 2A, 4 & Others)

Several State Public Service Commissions including TNPSC, APPSC, and TSPSC classify recruitment into numbered "Groups" based on post seniority, pay scale, and administrative responsibility. Understanding these groups helps candidates identify which exam to prepare for based on their qualification and career goals.

Group Typical Posts Minimum Qualification Selection Stages
Group 1 Deputy Collector, DSP, Assistant Commissioner, District Registrar Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains + Interview
Group 2 Assistant Section Officer, Tehsildar, Municipal Commissioner (Grade), Block Development Officer Bachelor's degree Prelims + Mains (some states include Interview)
Group 2A Junior Assistant, Bill Collector, Field Surveyor Bachelor's degree Written Exam (Certificate Verification)
Group 3 Various department Grade II/Non-Gazetted posts Varies by post Written Exam
Group 4 Junior Assistant, Typist, Steno-Typist, Bill Collector, Record Clerk, Village Administrative Officer (VAO) SSLC / 10th or 12th pass (varies by post) Single Written Exam (Certificate Verification)

Group numbering, post names, and minimum qualifications vary by state the table above reflects the common pattern used by TNPSC-style classification. Some states use different group labels or don't use numbered groups at all. Always confirm the exact group structure and eligibility on your state PSC's official notification.

Who Should Apply for Group 4?

Group 4 posts are typically entry-level government jobs open to candidates who have completed SSLC (10th) or Higher Secondary (12th), making them one of the most accessible and high-demand categories of PSC recruitment. These posts don't usually require a specific degree, have a single-stage written exam, and see some of the highest applicant volumes of any PSC exam due to the lower qualification bar and large number of annual vacancies.

State PSC Eligibility Criteria

There is no single eligibility rule for all State PSC jobs. Qualification, age limit, experience and other conditions differ depending on the commission and post.

Eligibility Criteria General Guidance
Educational Qualification Depends on the post and may include Diploma, Graduation, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Post Graduation or another prescribed qualification.
Age Limit Minimum and maximum age limits vary by commission and recruitment.
Age Relaxation Relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the recruitment.
State / Domicile Conditions State-specific eligibility, reservation, language or residency conditions may apply to certain recruitments.
Experience Some technical, teaching, specialist or senior posts require relevant professional experience.
Number of Attempts Attempt restrictions apply only where specifically prescribed for an examination or recruitment.

Important: Candidates should check the detailed recruitment notification before applying because eligibility conditions differ for every State PSC recruitment.

State PSC Selection Process

The State PSC selection process depends on the commission and the type of post. There is no single selection procedure followed for every PSC recruitment.

Depending on the recruitment, the selection process may include one or more of the following stages:

  • Preliminary Examination
  • Main Examination
  • Written Examination
  • Screening Test
  • Subject-specific Examination
  • Skill Test
  • Physical Test
  • Interview / Personality Test
  • Document Verification
  • Medical Examination

State Civil Services examinations may have Preliminary, Main and Interview stages, while technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitment may follow a different selection process.

Always check the individual recruitment notification for the exact examination and selection procedure.

How to Apply for State PSC Jobs 2026

The application process differs slightly between commissions, but candidates can generally follow these steps:

  1. Find the required State PSC recruitment from the latest jobs table above.
  2. Open the detailed recruitment page.
  3. Check the post name, vacancies, qualification, age limit, application fee and important dates.
  4. Read the official recruitment notification carefully.
  5. Open the official application website or application link.
  6. Complete registration or One-Time Registration if required by the commission.
  7. Enter the required personal, educational and category details.
  8. Upload the prescribed photograph, signature and supporting documents.
  9. Pay the application fee if applicable.
  10. Review the application before final submission.
  11. Submit the application before the specified last date.
  12. Save or print the submitted application for future reference.

Candidates should submit applications only through the application method specified in the official notification.

State PSC Exam Pattern and Syllabus

There is no common exam pattern or syllabus for all State PSC recruitments.

State Civil Services examinations generally cover broader subjects such as General Studies and state-specific topics, while technical, medical, engineering, teaching and departmental recruitment may focus more heavily on subjects related to the post.

The following can differ between recruitments:

  • Number of papers
  • Objective or descriptive examination
  • Total marks
  • Exam duration
  • Negative marking
  • Minimum qualifying marks
  • Language requirements
  • Subject-specific syllabus
  • Interview or skill test requirements

Candidates should refer to the syllabus and exam pattern issued for the specific State PSC recruitment they are applying for.

State PSC Jobs vs UPSC Jobs

State Public Service Commissions and the Union Public Service Commission conduct different recruitment processes.

State PSC UPSC
Conducts recruitment for posts and services connected with the respective state. Conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.
Recruitment rules differ from one State PSC to another. Recruitment is conducted under the rules applicable to UPSC examinations and vacancies.
May recruit for State Civil Services, engineering, medical, teaching, technical and departmental posts. Conducts Civil Services Examination and various other recruitment examinations for Union Government posts.

Candidates looking for Union Government recruitment through UPSC can visit the UPSC Jobs page.

PSC vs PCS - What Is the Difference?

PSC stands for Public Service Commission. It refers to the constitutional commission responsible for conducting recruitment for various government posts and services within its jurisdiction.

PCS commonly refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services posts and examinations.

A State Public Service Commission may conduct a State Civil Services or PCS examination, but it can also conduct recruitment for many other positions such as Medical Officer, Assistant Engineer, Lecturer, Agriculture Officer and departmental posts.

Therefore, State PSC Jobs covers a broader range of recruitment than only PCS or State Civil Services examinations.

How to Choose the Right State PSC Recruitment

Before applying for a State PSC vacancy, candidates should compare the recruitment requirements with their qualification and preferences.

Check the following details:

  • Required educational qualification
  • Age limit
  • Category and reservation conditions
  • State or language requirements, if any
  • Number of vacancies
  • Pay scale or salary
  • Job location
  • Application fee
  • Selection process
  • Examination pattern
  • Application deadline

Apply only after confirming that you meet the eligibility conditions mentioned in the official recruitment notification.

State PSC Recruitment Updates You Should Check

A recruitment notification can sometimes be followed by additional notices from the commission. Candidates should continue checking recruitment updates even after submitting their application.

Important updates may include:

  • Application date extension
  • Correction window
  • Vacancy revision
  • Exam date
  • Exam city information

  • Interview schedule

  • Final selection result

What are State PSC Jobs?

State PSC Jobs are government recruitment opportunities notified through State Public Service Commissions for various posts and services under state government departments.

Which State PSC jobs are currently open?

What qualification is required for State PSC jobs?

There is no single qualification required for all State PSC jobs. Depending on the post, candidates may need a Diploma, Graduation, Engineering degree, Medical qualification, Law degree, Post Graduation or another specified qualification.

Are all State PSC jobs for graduates?

No. Eligibility depends on the individual recruitment. Many administrative posts require a degree, while technical, professional and departmental posts may have different qualification requirements.

What is the age limit for State PSC jobs?

The minimum and maximum age limits vary according to the commission and post. Candidates should check the age criteria given in the individual recruitment notification.

Is age relaxation available for State PSC recruitment?

Age relaxation may be available to eligible categories according to the rules applicable to the respective recruitment. The exact relaxation should be checked in the official notification.

Is domicile compulsory for State PSC jobs?

Not for every State PSC recruitment. Some vacancies may have state-specific residency, reservation, language or other eligibility requirements. Candidates should check the relevant recruitment rules before applying.

What is the selection process for State PSC jobs?

The selection process varies by post. It may include a Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, written test, screening test, skill test, interview, physical test, document verification or medical examination.

Do all State PSC recruitments have Prelims and Mains?

No. Prelims and Mains are common in some State Civil Services examinations, but many technical, medical, teaching and departmental recruitments follow a different examination or selection process.

How can I apply for State PSC recruitment?

Open the required recruitment from the latest jobs table, read the eligibility and application details, check the official notification and use the official application link provided on the recruitment page.

What is the difference between State PSC and UPSC?

State PSCs conduct recruitment mainly for posts and services connected with their respective states, while UPSC conducts recruitment and examinations for various Union Government and All India Services posts.

Is PSC the same as PCS?

No. PSC means Public Service Commission, while PCS generally refers to Provincial Civil Service or State Civil Services. A State PSC can recruit for PCS as well as many other administrative, technical, medical and departmental posts.

Where can I check State PSC admit cards?

When an admit card is released, the related recruitment page should be updated with the admit card information and official download link. Candidates can also check the OnlyJobs Admit Card section.

What Is a Bharat Sarkari Job?

A Bharat Sarkari Job is any government job opportunity offered across India's central and state government departments - spanning all 28 states and 8 union territories. The term "Bharat" simply emphasises pan-India coverage: a Bharat Sarkari Job notification could originate from a central body like the SSC, UPSC, or Indian Railways, or from a state public service commission recruiting for state-level posts. Regardless of origin, these roles share the defining traits Indian aspirants seek - long-term job security, government pay scales, and statutory retirement benefits.

Sarkari Job vs Private Job

A sarkari job differs from private-sector employment in a few important ways: government positions are governed by service rules that protect against arbitrary termination, salaries follow Pay Commission recommendations rather than market negotiation, and employees are entitled to pension schemes (NPS or OPS depending on recruitment year), medical coverage under CGHS, and fixed working hours. Private jobs, by contrast, often offer higher starting pay in competitive fields but carry less structural job security.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

A Forest Guard helps protect forest areas, monitor activities, assist with wildlife conservation and report suspected forest offences. Duties can include patrolling assigned forest areas and supporting senior forest officials.

What is the qualification for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Some Forest Guard recruitments require Class 10 or Class 12 qualifications from a recognized board. However, the exact educational requirements depend on the state and recruitment notification.

Find the Forest Guard recruitment in the vacancy table above, open the detailed notification, confirm eligibility and follow the official application instructions.

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 - RFO Jobs

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 provides opportunities for candidates interested in forest administration, conservation and supervisory roles.

A Forest Range Officer, also referred to as a Range Forest Officer or RFO in some recruitment systems, may oversee forest protection activities, supervise field staff and manage responsibilities within an assigned forest range.

What is the qualification for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Forest Range Officer recruitment generally involves graduate-level eligibility. Some notifications require degrees in specified subjects such as science, agriculture, forestry or other approved disciplines.

The accepted qualifications vary by recruiting organization. A graduation degree alone does not automatically make a candidate eligible for every RFO vacancy.

How are Forest Range Officers selected?

Depending on the recruitment rules, selection may include:

  • Preliminary or main written examinations
  • Physical standards or fitness assessments
  • Interviews, where prescribed
  • Document verification
  • Medical examination

Candidates searching for RFO Vacancy 2026, Forest Ranger Recruitment or Forest Range Service Officer notifications should check the relevant vacancy details for exact eligibility and selection stages.

Forest-related vacancies are announced throughout the year by different recruiting organizations. Check the latest vacancy table above for the status of individual recruitments. An advertised post should be considered open only within its confirmed application period.

2. What is the last date for Forest Department Recruitment 2026?

3. How can I apply for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Find an applicable Forest Guard vacancy, review the educational and physical requirements, and follow the official application instructions before the closing date.

Some Forest Guard, Forest Watcher and support recruitments may accept Class 10 qualifications. Eligibility depends on the post and recruiting authority.

Yes, some Forest Guard recruitments accept Class 12 qualifications. Check the specific notification to confirm any subject or additional eligibility requirements.

6. Can graduates apply for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Graduates may qualify for certain Forest Range Officer vacancies, but some recruitments require degrees in specified disciplines. Candidates must verify the accepted qualifications.

Many Forest Guard, Forester and officer-level recruitments include written examinations. Other roles may use different selection methods. Follow the official selection process for the chosen vacancy.

A Forest Guard generally performs field-level protection and monitoring duties. A Forest Range Officer usually carries supervisory and administrative responsibilities for a forest range. Exact duties differ under the relevant service rules.

Eligible ex-servicemen can apply for vacancies where they meet the recruitment requirements. Reservation benefits and relaxations depend on the applicable rules.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

The Staff Selection Commission (SSC) has announced the proposed exam dates for the Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) Examination, 2026, commonly searched as SSC CPO SI. As per the Important Notice dated 01/10/2026 (F. No. HQ-EC033/7/2025-EC), the Computer Based Examination (CBE) is proposed between 20/11/2026 and 28/11/2026. The recruitment is for 1,871 tentative vacancies. Online applications closed on 30/09/2026.

When Is the SSC CPO SI Exam in 2026?

The SSC CPO SI CBE is proposed to be held from 20th to 28th November 2026. The Commission has described these as proposed dates, and the examination notice states that exam dates are tentative and any change will be communicated only through the Commission's website.

Educational Qualification

  • Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and Sub-Inspector (GD) in CAPFs: Bachelor's degree from a recognised university or equivalent. Final-year candidates could apply, provided they hold the qualification on or before the closing date for applications (30/09/2026).
  • Sub-Inspector (Fire) in CISF: Bachelor's degree in Science with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics, or Matriculation with a three-year Diploma in Mechanical, Civil, Electrical, Automobile, Chemical, Mining, Aeronautical or Telecommunication Engineering, or an equivalent qualification.

SSC CPO SI Selection Process 2026

The selection has four mandatory stages:

  1. Paper-I (Computer Based Examination)
  2. Physical Standard Test (PST) and Physical Endurance Test (PET)
  3. Paper-II (Computer Based Examination)
  4. Detailed Medical Examination (DME), followed by Document Verification by the CAPFs

Paper-I is of 1 hour, with a sectional timer of 15 minutes for each part.

Paper-II

Marking Scheme and Qualifying Marks

  • All questions are objective multiple choice. Parts I, II and III of both papers are in Hindi and English.
  • Negative marking is 0.25 marks per wrong answer in Paper-I and 0.50 marks per wrong answer in Paper-II.
  • Minimum qualifying marks in Paper-I and Paper-II (without NCC bonus marks): UR 30%, OBC/EWS 25%, all other categories 20%.
  • If the exam is held in multiple shifts, marks are normalised using the procedure published by the Commission.
  • NCC bonus marks in each paper: 5% of maximum marks for 'C' certificate, 3% for 'B' and 2% for 'A'.
  • The difficulty level of Paper-II will be higher than Paper-I.

SSC CPO SI Syllabus 2026

The notification gives an indicative syllabus for both papers.

  • General Intelligence and Reasoning: verbal and non-verbal reasoning such as analogies, classification, series, coding-decoding, Venn diagrams, space visualisation and critical thinking.
  • General Knowledge and General Awareness: current events, India and its neighbouring countries, history, culture, geography, economy, polity, Indian Constitution and scientific research.
  • Quantitative Aptitude: number system, percentage, ratio, averages, interest, profit and loss, time and work, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry and data interpretation.
  • English Comprehension: error recognition, fill in the blanks, vocabulary, grammar, sentence structure, synonyms, antonyms, idioms and comprehension.

How to Check SSC CPO SI Exam Date and Admit Card

  1. Visit the official SSC website at ssc.gov.in.
  2. Open the Notice Board and look for the notice dated 01/10/2026 on the Sub-Inspector in Delhi Police and CAPFs Examination, 2026.
  3. Download the notice PDF and check the proposed exam dates.
  4. About 10 days before the exam, check the website of your SSC Regional Office for the exam city and time table.
  5. Download the admit card from the Commission's website when it is released, normally 2 to 3 days before the exam, and take a printout.

Documents to Carry on Exam Day

  • Printout of the admit card (Admission Certificate)
  • Candidates who completed Aadhaar-based authentication: the notice says they will not be required to produce recent colour photographs and original photo ID at the exam venue.
  • Candidates who did not complete Aadhaar-based authentication: report 2 hours before the scheduled start, and carry two recent passport-size colour photographs and an original valid photo ID showing the date of birth printed on the admit card.
  • Accepted photo IDs include Voter ID, Driving Licence, PAN Card, Passport, school or college ID, Government or PSU employer ID card, and Ex-Serviceman Discharge Book.
  • If the photo ID has no date of birth, carry an additional original document that proves it, such as the Matriculation certificate or marks sheet.

Documents Required at Document Verification

Document Verification is conducted by the CAPFs before the final result. Candidates must bring originals and copies of documents such as:

  • Matriculation or Secondary certificate
  • Educational qualification certificate
  • Caste or category certificate, if applicable
  • Driving licence for motorcycle and car (male candidates opting for Delhi Police)
  • Ex-Servicemen, age-relaxation and departmental candidate certificates, if applicable
  • No Objection Certificate, if already employed in government service

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • The exam dates are proposed. Check the SSC website regularly, as the Commission is not bound to inform candidates individually by SMS, email or post.
  • Do not lock Aadhaar biometrics if you opted for Aadhaar-based authentication, as biometric verification is mandatory at different stages.
  • Keep a copy of your application form and exam documents for at least 3 years.
  • Post and force preferences are taken through an online option form after the Paper-II result. Once submitted, they are final and cannot be changed.
  • Candidature remains provisional until certificates and documents are verified by the appointing authority.
  • Unfair means can lead to cancellation of candidature and debarment from SSC exams.
  • For help, call the SSC toll-free helpline at 1800 309 3063.

What Is the India Post GDS Cut Off?

The GDS cut-off is the lowest Class 10 percentage among the candidates shortlisted in a given postal circle and category. India Post prepares separate merit lists for each circle and category directly from Class 10 marks. Candidates at or above that level are called for document verification.

  • No written exam or interview is part of the shortlisting.
  • Cut-offs differ across circles.
  • Each category (UR, OBC, EWS, SC, ST, PwBD) has its own cut-off.
  • The percentage is based on Class 10 marks. 
  • For grade-point boards, marks are converted with the formula: Marks = Grade Point x 9.5.

How Is the GDS Merit List Decided When Percentages Are Equal?

  • The older candidate is preferred.
  • If the tie continues, the Government of India's category rules apply in this order for women: ST, SC, OBC, EWS, then UR.
  • After that, the same category order applies for men: ST, SC, OBC, EWS, then UR.

How to Check the India Post GDS Cut Off 2026

  • Open the official website, www.indiapostgdsonline.gov.in.
  • Find the merit list or shortlisted candidates section for GDS Online Engagement Schedule-II, July 2026.
  • Choose your postal circle.
  • Download the circle-wise PDF.
  • Search for your registration number, which you received when you applied.

What Happens After the GDS Cut Off 2026?

  1. Merit list: Search your registration number in the circle-wise PDF.
  2. Document verification: Shortlisted candidates attend verification at the allotted postal division within 15 days.
  3. Appointment letter: Issued after successful verification.
  4. Basic training: Selected candidates complete training before starting duties.

How to Check the India Post GDS 1st Merit List 2026

  1. Go to indiapostgdsonline.gov.in.
  2. Open the link for the GDS July / Schedule-II 2026 shortlisted candidates (merit) list. The exact label can differ on the portal.
  3. Select your postal circle (state).
  4. Download the PDF.
  5. Press Ctrl+F and search by registration number or name.

How to Check the GDS Merit List Without a Registration Number

Search your name in the circle PDF and confirm the match using your post, division and marks details. Use the registration number from your application if you have it, because many candidates share similar names.

Details Mentioned in the Merit List PDF

  • Registration number and candidate name
  • Post and division / unit
  • Merit details based on Class 10 marks
  • Document verification instructions

India Post GDS Selection Process

  • There is no written exam or interview.
  • The merit list is system-generated from Class 10 marks of a recognised board.
  • Marks are aggregated and converted to a percentage up to four decimal places, as described for earlier GDS cycles.
  • Shortlisted candidates go through document verification before provisional engagement.

Documents Required for GDS Document Verification

  • Class 10 marksheet
  • Valid ID proof
  • Proof of date of birth
  • Medical certificate
  • EWS certificate, if applicable

What to Do After Your Name Appears in the Merit List

  1. Download and save your circle's PDF.
  2. Read the verification instructions and the deadline in the list.
  3. Collect originals and copies of your documents.
  4. Report to the authority named against your name within the stated date.

What If Your Name Is Not in the 1st Merit List?

You are not shortlisted in this list, but more lists can follow if vacancies remain. In the 2023 Schedule-II cycle, for example, four merit lists were released. No second list date is announced for 2026. Keep checking the official portal.

India Post GDS Cut Off 2026

No official cut-off is published. Shortlisting is merit-based and the last selected percentage varies by circle, division, post and category. Check the marks of shortlisted candidates in your circle's PDF.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Use only the official portal. Do not pay anyone for selection.
  • Make sure you open the Schedule-II, July 2026 list, not the January 2026 list.
  • Carry original documents to verification.
  • Check dates and deadlines in the official PDF, not on third-party sites.
