UPSC Advt 12/2026 Vacancy Details (Category-wise)

Post Total Reservation PwBD Status
Junior Technical Officer (Sugar Technology) 01 OBC-01 Not reserved; suitable for OL/OA (one leg/arm affected) categories only
Assistant Legislative Counsel (Grade IV, ILS) 08 UR-04, EWS-01, OBC-02, SC-01 1 post reserved for PwBD (Blindness/Low Vision category only); also suitable for ASD-Mild

Note: "Suitable but not reserved" means a PwBD candidate meeting the 40%+ disability criterion in the listed sub-category may apply and will be considered under the general standard of merit, without a dedicated reservation. Each post's advertisement carries a detailed PwBD sub-category table (blindness/low vision, deaf/hard of hearing, various locomotor conditions, autism/intellectual/learning/mental illness, and multiple disabilities); only the categories marked "Yes" for suitability/reservation in the official notification apply to that specific post.

UPSC Advt 12/2026 Eligibility (Post-wise)

1. Junior Technical Officer (Sugar Technology)

  • Degree in Science or Engineering from a recognized University/Institute, with Associateship in Sugar Technology OR Post-graduate Diploma in Sugar Technology
  • Experience: 3 years' teaching/research/advisory experience in Sugar Technology, OR 3 years' practical experience in a sugar factory in a managerial capacity
  • Desirable: M.Sc. (Chemistry) or M.Tech (Sugar Technology); experience in drafting/editing scientific and technological reports

2. Assistant Legislative Counsel (Grade IV, ILS)

A Degree in Law from a recognized University or equivalent, AND one of: 7+ years as a member of a State Judicial Service; OR 7+ years in a superior post in a State's legal department; OR 7+ years as a Central Government servant with legal-affairs experience; OR a Master's Degree in Law with 5+ years of teaching/research experience in Law; OR a qualified legal practitioner of at least 30 years of age (7+ years as advocate/pleader, or 5+ years as a High Court attorney in Bombay/Calcutta, or a combined 5+ years as attorney and advocate).

Desirable: experience in legislative drafting (preference given if the post is in the Legislative Department).

3. Law Officer

  • Degree in Law from a recognized Institute/University
  • 2 years' experience in legal work as a Legal Practitioner, OR 2 years' legal-work experience in a Government office

4. Specialist Grade II (Junior Scale) – Cardiology

  • A recognized medical qualification under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 (First/Second Schedule or Part-II of Third Schedule, other than a licentiate qualification)
  • Post-graduate degree in Cardiology (D.M. Cardiology) or equivalent
  • 3 years' experience in Cardiology after obtaining the post-graduate degree
Note: All qualifications are relaxable at UPSC's discretion, for reasons recorded in writing, for candidates who are otherwise well qualified.

UPSC Advt 12/2026 Age Limit

Post Age Limit (as on closing date)
Junior Technical Officer (Sugar Technology) 38 years (OBC); +10 years further relaxable for PwBD
Assistant Legislative Counsel 40 years (UR/EWS), 43 years (OBC), 45 years (SC); +10 years further relaxable for PwBD
Law Officer 30 years (UR), 33 years (OBC); +10 years further relaxable for PwBD
Specialist Grade II (Cardiology) 48 years (OBC); +10 years further relaxable for PwBD

General Age Relaxation (All Posts)

  • The listed age limit is normal for EWS/UR; relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, and 10 years for PwBD, in respect of vacancies reserved for them
  • Ex-Servicemen/Commissioned Officers: 5 years' relaxation (subject to at least 6 months' continuous service after attestation as on the closing date)
  • Central/UT Government servants: up to 5 years (10 years for SC/ST, 8 years for OBC posts reserved for them), subject to 3 years' continuous service in an allied cadre
  • PwBD candidates: 10 years' relaxation (so SC/ST-PwBD get up to 15 years total, OBC-PwBD up to 13 years total), subject to maximum age on closing date not exceeding 56 years; disability must be 40% or more

Assistant Legislative Counsel Level-11 Group "A" Gazetted, Grade-IV Indian Legal Service; permanent; probation 2 years
Law Officer Level-07 General Central Service Group "B" Gazetted, Non-Ministerial; permanent; probation 2 years + mandatory 2-week induction training
Specialist Grade II (Cardiology) Level-11 plus NPA Group "A" Gazetted, Non-Ministerial; permanent; probation 1 year; private practice prohibited (NPA given instead)

UPSC Advt 12/2026 Selection Process

Selection is by interview, or by a Recruitment Test (RT)/Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) followed by interview, depending on the number of applications received for a post. There is no fixed CBT syllabus published for these posts in the advertisement.

  • Where applications are numerous, UPSC may apply shortlisting criteria: higher desirable qualifications, higher-than-minimum educational qualification, higher-than-minimum relevant experience, experience before/after acquiring essential qualification, experience not otherwise prescribed, or a Recruitment Test
  • Minimum level of suitability at interview (out of 100 marks): UR–50, OBC–45, SC/ST/PH–40
  • Where an RT precedes the interview, candidates must clear the minimum suitability level at both stages; the RT qualifying level is decided case-by-case by UPSC
  • Where an RT/CRT is held, it will ordinarily be conducted at: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam (Leh/Kargil/Srinagar/Delhi for Ladakh UT posts)
  • Candidature is provisional at every stage; mere fulfilment of minimum qualification/experience does not guarantee a call for interview
  • Where sufficient eligible PwBD candidates are not available for exclusively-reserved posts, the experience requirement (years, not nature) may be relaxed up to 50%

How to Apply for UPSC Advt 12/2026

  1. Visit upsconline.nic.in and create an account, if not already registered.
  2. Complete Universal Registration (generates a Universal Registration Number, or URN, common across all UPSC recruitments) and the Common Application Form (CAF).
  3. Fill the post/vacancy-specific fourth module for the post you are applying to; this generates a post-specific Application Number.
  4. Upload your photograph and capture a live photo as part of the CAF; sign three times on plain white paper in black ink and upload the signature.
  5. Upload supporting documents separately against each claim (date of birth, category, qualification, experience, etc.) as individual PDFs – do not upload pay slips, resumes, appointment/relieving letters, or unsigned experience certificates in this module.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹25 online (Visa/Master/RuPay Card, UPI, or net banking), if applicable to your category.
  7. Review all entries carefully – no correction, alteration, or withdrawal is allowed after final submission.
  8. Submit before the closing date: 16 October 2026, 1800 hrs.
  9. Take a printout of the finally submitted application; you are not required to send this to UPSC by post, but must bring it (with original documents) if called for interview.

Application Fee

Category Fee
Unreserved / OBC / EWS (Male) ₹25
Women (all categories) / SC / ST / PwBD Exempted (Nil)
Important: Fee once paid is non-refundable and cannot be held in reserve for another exam/selection. Applications without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation/10th standard certificate or mark sheet showing date of birth
  • Degree/Diploma certificate as proof of educational qualification (or provisional certificate plus all mark sheets, if the final certificate is not yet issued)
  • Order/letter proving equivalence, if claiming a qualification as "equivalent" to the one prescribed
  • Experience certificate(s) in the prescribed proforma from the Head of Organisation/Department, clearly stating dates, pay, and nature of duties (part-time/daily-wage/guest-faculty experience is not counted)
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC) in the prescribed proforma from a competent authority; OBC candidates must also submit a non-creamy-layer declaration as on the closing date
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed proforma from a duly constituted Medical Board, for PwBD candidates
  • Certificate/document for age relaxation (Ex-servicemen, Central/UT Government employees, or special provisions), as applicable
  • Declaration by candidates already in regular Government service, confirming they have informed their Head of Office/Department of this application
  • Name-change documents (marriage/remarriage/divorce or other), if applicable
  • Certified translation (by a Gazetted Officer or notary) for any document not in Hindi or English

Important Conditions

  • Citizenship: Indian citizen, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee (pre-1962), or a person of Indian origin migrated from certain specified countries with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India
  • A candidate applying under UR cannot later claim a reserved category; requests to switch between reserved categories are not entertained; PwBD candidates cannot change their disability sub-category
  • Reserved-category candidates who fail to substantiate their claim by the prescribed stage will be considered against unreserved vacancies if they otherwise meet UR conditions
  • Mobile phones, smart watches, pen drives, cameras, Bluetooth devices, etc. are strictly banned in the examination/interview hall
  • Face authentication and identity verification are mandatory at the examination venue/interview hall
  • Scribe facility is available for specified PwBD categories (blindness, both-arms-affected locomotor disability, cerebral palsy automatically; others on production of a medical certificate)
  • Furnishing false particulars, impersonation, using unfair means, or misconduct can lead to disqualification, debarment (permanent or for a specified period) from UPSC exams and Central Government employment, and disciplinary/criminal action
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify a candidate
  • Outstation candidates called for interview at UPSC are reimbursed travel expenses restricted to Second/Sleeper Class train fare, paid via NEFT/bank transfer
  • Summoning for interview does not guarantee selection; UPSC may recommend higher initial pay for meritorious candidates
  • For the Law Officer post, GNCTD's own OBC reservation rules apply (a valid GNCTD-recognized OBC certificate, or one traceable to a GNCTD-issued family certificate for those settled in Delhi before 8 September 1993, is required)

Punjab & Sind Bank, Human Resource Development Deptt has announced 1 vacancy for the post of Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) on a contract basis. The engagement is for a fixed contractual tenure of minimum three years, extendable at Bank's discretion, and is purely contractual without conferring any right to claim regular employment. Candidates holding a Graduate or equivalent degree from a reputed Govt. recognized University and must be CAIIB are eligible to apply. The compensation and terms & conditions are negotiable depending upon the suitability of the candidate. Eligible applicants can submit the ONLINE application from 15 October 2026 to 30 October 2026 through the Bank's website. The selection process involves preliminary scrutiny, shortlisting, and personal interaction or interview before the Selection Committee.

Punjab & Sind Bank Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) at a Glance

Particulars Details
Organisation Punjab & Sind Bank
Department or Unit Human Resource Development Department (H.O. HRD Dept.)
Post Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)
Vacancies 1
Pay Negotiable depending upon the suitability of the candidate
Contract Term Minimum 3 years (extendable at Bank's discretion)
Experience Required 15 years in banking or financial services (minimum 5 years in Audit / Finance / Compliance / Legal / Risk Management)
Job Location Head Office/Corporate Office (transferable to any office in India)
How to Apply Online through the Bank's website
Last Date 30.10.2026
Selection Preliminary scrutiny, shortlisting, and personal interaction/interview

Who Can Apply

Candidates must meet the following nationality, qualification, and age criteria to be eligible for the Punjab & Sind Bank Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) position:

  • Nationality: Must be a Citizen of India, a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, a Tibetan Refugee who came over to India before 1st Jan 1962, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries with an eligibility certificate issued by the Govt. of India.
  • Mandatory Educational Qualifications: Must be a Graduate or have an equivalent degree from a reputed Govt. recognized University and must be CAIIB.
  • Mandatory Experience: 15 years in the banking or financial services, out of which a minimum of five years shall be in the Audit / Finance / Compliance / Legal / Risk Management functions. (Risk management functions include control functions within business lines; regional/zonal/business heads with requisite responsibility in control functions for five years or more are also eligible).
  • Desirable Qualifications: Additional qualifications such as Ph.D. / MBA / LLM / CA / CMA / CS / CFA or Diploma / Degree in Compliance and Ethics or its equivalent. Preference will be given to candidates with these additional qualifications.
  • Age Limit: Minimum 40 years of age and less than 55 years of age as on 01.10.2026, including all relaxations.

Pay and Terms

The compensation and terms & conditions will be negotiated and finalized depending upon the suitability of the candidate. The Chief Compliance Officer is engaged for a fixed contractual tenure of minimum three years, which can be extended at the Bank's discretion subject to satisfactory performance. The engagement is purely contractual and does not attract provisions of PF, Gratuity, or Pension, and no allowances, payments, benefits, or facilities other than those mentioned in the terms are payable. Working hours, weekly offs, and holidays are applicable as per serving employees of the bank. The selected officer is entitled to 30 days of paid leave per calendar year (not more than 5 days at a time); absences exceeding 30 days in a contract year lead to proportionate deductions from the consolidated payment.

Punjab & Sind Bank Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) Job Description

The Chief Compliance Officer assists senior management in effectively managing compliance risks faced by the bank. The core responsibilities include:

  • Designing and maintaining a compliance framework, conducting compliance training on regulatory and conduct risks, and communicating compliance expectations.
  • Apprising the Board and senior management on regulations, rules, standards, and developments, and providing clarification on compliance issues.
  • Conducting compliance risk assessments at least once a year, developing a risk-oriented activity plan for ACB approval, and reporting promptly on major changes, failures, or breaches.
  • Monitoring and periodically testing compliance, examining sustenance of compliance, and ensuring time-bound compliance with supervisory observations made by the RBI.
  • Framing and implementing a comprehensive Compliance Policy and Compliance Manual for the Bank, and vetting guidelines and circulars before dissemination.
  • Interacting frequently with Legal, Operational Risk Management, Taxation, and Audit/Inspection departments, and submitting quarterly/annual reviews to the Board.
  • Serving as the nodal point of contact between the bank and the RBI, participating in quarterly informal discussions, and ensuring compliance with overseas branch regulations and FEMA requirements.
  • Acting as a member of the 'new product' committees to ensure new products and processes have clearance from all perspectives including compliance.

How to Apply for Punjab & Sind Bank Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)

  1. Log on to the Bank's website at https://punjabandsind.bank.in/ and navigate to the "Recruitment" link on the Home Page.
  2. Ensure you have scanned copies of your photograph, signature, thumb impression, hand-written declaration, education certificates, experience certificates, and DOB proof in the specified formats (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .bmp, .gif for images; PDF for documents).
  3. Fill out the online application form with correct details matching your certificates and identity proof.
  4. Pay the non-refundable application fee of Rs. 1000/- plus applicable GST (Total fee Rs. 1180/- including CGST and SGST for New Delhi, or IGST for out of New Delhi) via the ONLINE mode only.
  5. Submit the completed online application form before the last date of 30.10.2026 and retain a copy for future reference and interview verification.

Selection Process

The selection process for the Chief Compliance Officer post comprises:

  • Preliminary Scrutiny: Checking applications with reference to age, qualifications, experience, and other eligibility conditions.
  • Shortlisting: Shortlisting candidates based on relevant experience, seniority, professional credentials, academic track record, and suitability.
  • Personal Interaction / Interview: An interview before a duly constituted Selection Committee assessing knowledge of credit, market, operational, liquidity, technology, cyber, climate risks, leadership ability, independence of judgement, and regulatory awareness.
  • Verification: Verification of credentials, vigilance status, integrity, reputation, and antecedents, followed by medical fitness and background checks. Final selection is based on marks obtained in the interview process according to merit ranking.

Punjab & Sind Bank Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) Important Instructions

  • Applications must be submitted online through the official website between 15.10.2026 and 30.10.2026. No other mode of application is accepted.
  • Application fee is non-refundable and must be paid online. Cash, demand drafts, cheques, and money orders are not accepted.
  • Candidates must produce original educational certificates, mark sheets, and experience certificates at the time of document verification and interview.
  • Serving candidates in Government or Public Sector Undertakings including banks must produce a "No Objection Certificate" from their employer at the time of interview.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to immediate disqualification of the candidate.
  • The selected candidate will be posted preferably at the Head Office/Corporate Office, though the bank reserves the right to post them anywhere in India.

Cochin Shipyard (CSL AN Ship Repair Unit - CANSRU) has announced 6 vacancies for Graduate Apprentice (Electronics & Communication Engg.), Technician (Diploma) Apprentice (Mechanical Engg.), Technician (Diploma) Apprentice (Electrical Engg), and Technician (Diploma) Apprentice (Electronics and Communication Engg.) posts under its 2026 recruitment. The apprenticeship training duration will be for a period of one year on a contract basis, offering stipends of Rs. 15,000 per month and Rs. 13,000 per month by post. Eligible candidates can apply online from 14 October 2026 to 30 October 2026. The selection process involves short-listing based on percentage of marks obtained in basic prescribed qualification, certificate verification of short-listed candidates, and provisional selection subject to medical fitness.

Cochin Shipyard Recruitment 2026 Quick Facts

Particulars Details
Establishment Cochin Shipyard
Seats 6
Trades Electronics & Communication Engg, Mechanical Engg, Electrical Engg
Stipend Rs. 15,000/- (Graduate) and Rs. 13,000/- (Technician) per month
Training Period 1 Year
Who Can Apply Indian citizens domiciled in Andaman & Nicobar Islands
Age Limit Above 18 years old as on 30.10.2026
Apply At nats.education.gov.in
Last Date 30.10.2026

Seats by Trade

The notification details the training seats across Graduate and Technician (Diploma) apprentice categories as follows:

S.No. Discipline Number of Training Seats Stipend per Month
Category – I Graduate Apprentices
1 Electronics & Communication Engg. 1 ₹15,000/-
Category – II Technician (Diploma) Apprentices
1 Mechanical Engg. 3 ₹13,000/-
2 Electrical Engg 1
3 Electronics and Communication Engg. 1
Total 5 -

Who Can Apply

Qualification

Candidates must possess the relevant minimum educational qualifications specified for each category:

  • Category – I Graduate Apprentices: A Degree in Engineering or Technology granted by a Statutory University or an Institution empowered to grant such degree by an Act of Parliament in relevant discipline, or Graduate examination of Professional bodies recognised by State or Central Government as equivalent.
  • Category – II Technician (Diploma) Apprentices: A Diploma in Engineering or Technology granted by a State Council or Board of Technical Education established by a State Government, a University, or an Institution recognised by the State or Central Government in relevant discipline.
  • Candidates with equivalent qualifications must submit an Equivalency Certificate issued by the competent authority.
  • For conversion of Aggregate Grade Points (CGPA/OGPA/CPI) where criteria are undefined by the University/Institute, grade points must be multiplied by 10 to obtain the required percentage.

Age

Candidates must be above 18 years old as on 30.10.2026.

Who Cannot Apply

Candidates who have already undergone or are currently undergoing apprenticeship under the Apprentices (Amendment) Act 1973 in any Government, Public Sector, or Private Organisation are NOT ELIGIBLE to apply.

Reservation

Government of India Directives on reservation applicable for Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Other Backward Class (OBC), and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) will be strictly followed.

Stipend and Training Period

The duration of the apprenticeship training is one year as per the Apprentices (Amendment) Act 1973. Category I Graduate Apprentices receive a stipend of ₹15,000/- per month, while Category II Technician (Diploma) Apprentices receive ₹13,000/- per month. No travel expenses, boarding, or lodging will be provided by CSL during the training period.

How to Apply for Cochin Shipyard Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official apprenticeship portal at nats.education.gov.in.
  2. For students registered in the old portal (portal.mhrdnats.gov.in), activate the account using the forgot password option at the student login page, then log in and complete the application form.
  3. For students with no prior registration, click on Student, select Student Register, complete the application form, and obtain the unique Enrolment Number.
  4. Log in to the portal and search for "COCHIN SHIPYARD LIMITED" under "Apply against advertised vacancies".
  5. Click Apply to submit the application and verify that the status reads "applied".

Selection Process

Selection is based on short-listing of candidates according to the percentage of marks obtained in the basic prescribed qualification for the respective disciplines. Candidates with the same percentage of marks will be ranked based on seniority in the passing year. Short-listed candidates must attend certificate verification with original and self-attested copies of proof of age, qualification, marks, caste, and disability (if applicable). Final provisional selection is subject to medical fitness.

Last Date of Online Application 30.10.2026

Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) has notified 42 contractual vacancies for Sr. Section Engineer/Inspection/Electrical (25) and Sr. Section Engineer/Inspection/Mech (17) posts. Eligible candidates can apply through email or post on or before 9 November 2026. Applicants must be Sr. Section Engineers in Pay Level-7 with a minimum of 5 years of experience, while a Degree or Diploma is preferred. The pay is specified as Pay Level-7 for both posts, with a 4-year tenure that is extendable or curtailable. Selection involves screening by a committee based on APAR and educational qualification, followed by merit list preparation.

Applications must reach through proper channel to the Director General, RDSO, Manak Nagar, Lucknow-226011 on or before 09.11.2026 by e-mail or Post etc. The official email address for application submission is [email protected].

  • Sr. Section Engineer (Cadre Post) Pay Level-7 working in the concerned department (Electrical or Mechanical) of Zonal Railway/Production Unit.

Selection will be based on the screening of eligible candidates by a Screening Committee. Screening will be conducted based on prescribed marks for two items: APAR of last 03 years (Maximum Marks: 15) and Educational/Professional Qualifications (Maximum Marks: 05). Oil India is recruiting candidates for 1 vacancy for the Contractual Warden (Female) for School of Nursing post on a contract basis. Eligible candidates can attend a walk-in for Personal Assessment on 28 October 2026, with reporting at 7:00 AM at Occupational Health Centre, OIL Hospital, Oil India Limited, Duliajan, Assam. Applicants must bring a filled Personal Bio-Data Form along with original and self-attested copies of all required documents. The engagement offers fixed emoluments of Rs. 24,960.00 fixed per month plus Rs. 960.00 per day based on attendance, with initial tenure for 06 months extendable up to 24 months. The selection process consists of a Walk-in for Personal Assessment carrying a total of 100 marks, with qualifying marks set at 50.

Candidates must report for mandatory registration at the venue between 07:00 A.M. and 09:00 A.M. on 28/10/2026. No candidate will be allowed to register beyond this time frame. Only eligible candidates with original documents will appear for the Walk-in for Personal Assessment, which is evaluated out of a total of 100 marks with a qualifying mark of 50. Public Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) for Power Finance Corporation Limited (PFC) has officially released the Chairman & Managing Director Recruitment 2026 notification (Advt. No. 109/2026) for 1 vacancy. Eligible internal and external candidates meeting the prescribed employment status, pay scale, and eligibility criteria, with a minimum age of 45 years, can apply online up to 9 November 2026 through the PESB application portal. The selected candidate will be appointed to a leadership position with a pay scale of ₹2,00,000–₹3,70,000 (IDA). Candidates should review the official notification for detailed eligibility criteria and application instructions before submitting their applications.

On the date of occurrence of vacancy (01.05.2027), the age of superannuation is 60 years. (ii) The applicants should possess cumulative experience of at least 5 years in core HR/IR/Personnel Management along with at least 3 years cumulative experience during the last 10 years in Finance or Business Development or Production or Operations or Marketing or Project Management in a large organization of repute. The applicant must, on the date of application, as well as on the date of interview, be employed in a regular capacity – and not in a contractual/ad-hoc capacity – in one of the following: Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) including a full-time functional Director on the Board; Central Government Group 'A' Officers including the Armed Forces of the Union and All India Services and officers from Public Sector Banks/ Financial Institutions/ Autonomous Bodies, etc.; State Public Sector Enterprise (SPSE) where annual turnover is Rs. 10,000 crore or more; Private Sector Company/ Joint Venture (JV) [50:50 JVs of Central Government/ State Governments and JVs of CPSEs with other CPSEs/ organisations (50:50 JVs)]/ National and State level Cooperative Federations whose annual turnover is Rs. 10,000 crore or more. CRPF Sportsperson Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Post Educational Qualification
HC/GD (Sports Quota) 10+2 or equivalent from a recognized Board/University recognized by the Central or State Government, or equivalent Army Qualification (for Ex-Army personnel)
CT/GD (Sports Quota) Matriculation or its equivalent from a recognized Board

Candidates who do not possess the prescribed educational qualification as on 11 November 2026 are not eligible to apply. Educational and sports qualification certificates other than from a Central/State Board must be accompanied by a Government notification declaring the equivalence of that qualification for Central Government service.

Sports Qualification – HC/GD

  • Represented the country in a recognized International Competition/Meet, with clearance from the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
  • Represented a State/UT in the National Games/Championship organized by a National Sports Federation recognized by the Department of Sports, or in National Games organized by the Indian Olympic Association, with a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  • Secured 1st or 2nd position in an individual event in Inter-University Tournaments (for team events, the team must have reached the finals) conducted by the Association of Indian Universities (AIU)/Inter University Sports Board.
  • Won Gold or Silver medal in an individual/team event at Junior National level Games/Championship/Meet organized by a recognized National Sports Federation.

Sports Qualification – CT/GD

  • Represented a State in Senior/Junior National level Games/Championships organized by a recognized National Sports Federation.
  • Represented a State School Team in National Sports/Games for Schools conducted by the All-India School Games Federation of India (SGFI), with a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  • Represented a State/UT in Khelo India University Games/Khelo India Youth Games/Khelo India Winter Games, with a medal or position up to 3rd place.
  • Represented their University in Inter-University Tournaments conducted by the Inter-University Sports Boards, in any sport/game.
Note: The sports achievement/certificate must be from within the last two years from the date of publication of this advertisement (i.e., achievements between 30 September 2024 and 30 September 2026 are eligible). Candidates awaiting results, or not in possession of the required educational/sports certificates, are not eligible and need not apply.

CRPF Sportsperson Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection proceeds through Identity Check, Documentation, Physical Standard Test (PST), Sports Trial Test, and Detailed/Review Medical Examination, in sequence.

1. Documentation

All candidates undergo document verification, producing original documents/certificates relating to age, education, sports achievement, domicile and category. Candidates unable to produce the prescribed originals are eliminated at this stage; those qualified proceed to the PST.

2. Marking of Achievements (Merit List Basis)

Marks are awarded for the single highest medal/position achieved during the eligible window (30 September 2024 to 30 September 2026); if a candidate has more than one medal, only the highest-scoring one counts. Sample marking tiers:

Competition Level Gold Silver Bronze Participation
Olympic Games (Summer/Winter) 100 96 92 80
World Championship/World Cup 90 86 82 70
Asian/Commonwealth Games 80 76 72 60
Asian/Commonwealth Championship or Cup 70 66 62 50
Youth Olympic Games 60 56 52 40
Youth/Junior World Championship or Cup 55 51 47 35
Youth/Junior Asian & Commonwealth Championship 50 46 42 30
SAF Games / recognized International Competition (min. 7 countries, backed by a National-level medal) 40 36 32 26
National Games/Senior National Championship – Individual medal 30 26 22 12
National Games/Senior National Championship – Team event 26 22 18 8
Youth/Junior National Championship/Inter-University/Khelo India – Individual medal 20 16 12 6
Youth/Junior National Championship/Inter-University/Khelo India – Team event 16 12 8 4

3. Physical Standard Test (PST)

Standard Male Female
Height 170 cm 157 cm
Chest (male only) 80 cm unexpanded, min. 5 cm expansion —
Weight Proportionate to height and age, as per medical standards

Height/chest relaxations are available for several categories, including Scheduled Tribes (162.5/150 cm), ST candidates of North-Eastern States (157/147.5 cm), ST candidates of Left-Wing Extremism-affected districts (160/147.5 cm), Garhwalis/Kumaonis/Dogras/Marathas and candidates from Assam, Himachal Pradesh, J&K and Ladakh (165/155 cm), candidates from the North-Eastern States of Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura (162.5/152.5 cm), and candidates from the Gorkha Territorial Administration area of Darjeeling district (157/152.5 cm), with corresponding chest relaxations for male candidates in several of these categories.

4. Sports Trial Test

Candidates who qualify the PST undergo the Sports Trial Test, conducted by a Board of Officers. This test is purely qualifying (pass/fail) – no marks are awarded, and total marks for the merit list come only from the achievement marking scheme above. Candidates may be subjected to a Dope Test on the day of the trial; no appeal for re-conduct of the trial test is entertained.

5. Detailed Medical Examination (DME) & Review Medical Examination (RME)

Conducted per the Uniform Guidelines for Recruitment Medical Examination for GOs and NGOs in CAPFs and AR (MHA U.O. No. A.VI-1/2014-Rectt(SSB) dated 20.05.2015 and MHA OM No. E.32012/ADG(Med)/DME/RME/DA-1/2020(Part file)/1166 dated 31.05.2021, as amended). Minimum distance vision required is 6/6 and 6/9 in both eyes without correction; colour-blind candidates are not eligible; candidates must not have knock knee, flat foot, varicose veins or squint. Tattoos are restricted in content (secular/religious symbols only, as per Indian Army norms), location (left forearm inner aspect or dorsum of hands only) and size (less than ¼ of that body part). Candidates declared unfit in DME may undergo RME.

Order of Preference (for Merit)

Where marks are comparable, preference follows this order: (a) International representation with Department of Sports clearance; (b) Senior/Junior National Championship representation with a medal (Senior preferred over Junior); (c) Inter-University/Khelo India University Games medal; (d) Khelo India Youth/Winter Games medal; (e) School National Games medal; (f) participation at levels (b)–(e) without a medal, in the same order.

How to Apply for CRPF Sportsperson Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit rect.crpf.gov.in and read the instructions carefully before filling the application.
  2. Create your profile and upload a copy of the certificate/document for your sports discipline, in support of your highest medal/position or highest level of participation, before applying – applications without this upload will be rejected during scrutiny.
  3. Fill the online application form and pay the application fee (where applicable) through the website only.
  4. Submit the application before 11 November 2026, 23:59 hrs.
  5. Use the correction window (12–14 November 2026) if you need to modify your submitted application.
Important: The application must be submitted ONLINE only; no offline application is accepted, and candidature of anyone submitting offline will be summarily rejected. Candidates serving in Government/Semi-Government departments must submit their application through their employer along with a No Objection Certificate (as per Annexure-A format) – applications without an NOC will not be accepted.

Documents Required (Original, at Document Verification)

  • Educational certificates, Sports certificates, Domicile and Caste certificates, etc.
  • Matriculation/10th class certificate, for verification of Date of Birth
  • OBC (NCL) Certificate (Annexure-F), SC/ST Certificate (Annexure-G), or EWS Certificate valid for 2026-27 (Annexure-H), as applicable – certificates in any other format are not accepted
  • Undertaking for OBC (NCL) reservation claim, as per Annexure-F
  • No Objection Certificate (Annexure-B), for candidates serving in Government service, produced at the time of physical document verification
  • Certificate for claiming height/chest relaxation (Annexure-I), if applicable
  • Four latest passport-size photographs, matching the one submitted with the application form

Important Conditions

  • Application Fee: Male candidates belonging to UR/OBC/EWS pay Rs. 100/- through the recruitment website; the fee is exempted for all female candidates and for SC/ST/Ex-Servicemen candidates. The fee is neither refunded nor adjusted against any other recruitment process, under any circumstances.
  • Selected candidates must submit a bond to serve the Force for a minimum of 3 years (or a specific period as prescribed), backed by an undertaking bond of Rs. 1,00,000/-, to promote sports in the Force, before they can resign for better employment elsewhere or on any other ground.
  • Posts carry All India service liability; selected candidates are liable to serve anywhere in India or abroad, and will be governed by the CRPF Act 1949 and Rules 1955.
  • CRPF reserves the right to modify, cancel, postpone, or reschedule any stage of the recruitment process, and to change the sequence of the recruitment procedure, without assigning any reason.
  • Submitting fabricated documents, or documents that have been tampered with, will lead to cancellation of candidature at any stage, including at the time of document verification or later.
  • The Board of Officers may also recommend cases of Outstanding Sportspersons who show excellent trial performance but require some relaxation in height/chest/weight for their sport, subject to approval by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The source describes one stage for the Apprentice recruitment: an online examination. Candidates apply, appear for the online objective test, and the exam is the stage the syllabus and pattern below are built around.

  1. Online Application: Eligible candidates apply against the 530 vacancies.

UCO Bank Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

Online Exam Pattern

The paper has 100 objective questions carrying 100 marks, to be attempted in 60 minutes. Each of the four sections has 25 questions and 25 marks.

Section Questions Marks
General/Financial Awareness 25 25
General English 25 25
Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude 25 25
Quantitative Aptitude 25 25
Total 100 100

Also Read: DSSSB Various Post Final Answer Key 2026

UCO Bank Apprentice Syllabus 2026

The topic lists below cover the sections for which a syllabus is available. They are grouped by sub-area so you can plan your study around them.

1. General English

  • Vocabulary: Synonyms, antonyms, one-word substitutions
  • Grammar: Spotting errors, sentence correction, active/passive voice, direct/indirect speech
  • Comprehension: Reading comprehension, passage completion, rearrangement of passage topics
  • Usage: Phrases and idioms, homonyms

2. Reasoning Ability

  • Sequences and order: Number and alphabetic series, ranking and time sequence, direction and distance
  • Logical reasoning: Syllogism, statements and conclusions, assumptions and arguments
  • Puzzles and arrangements: Coding-decoding, blood relations, seating arrangements, input/output
  • Miscellaneous: Odd one out, alphanumeric series, decision making

3. Quantitative Aptitude

  • Arithmetic basics: Ratio and proportion, averages, percentages, simple and compound interest
  • Applied arithmetic: Time, speed and distance; time and work; mixture and alligation; stocks and shares
  • Advanced topics: Heights and distances, logarithms, permutation and combination, probability
  • Data Interpretation: Tables, charts and graphs

4. General/Financial Awareness

This section carries 25 questions and 25 marks. A topic-wise syllabus is not specified in the source. Check the official UCO Bank notification for the detailed list.

5. Computer Aptitude

Computer Aptitude is paired with Reasoning Ability in a single 25-question section. A separate topic list for computer aptitude is not specified in the source.

How to Prepare for UCO Bank Apprentice Exam 2026

  1. Map the syllabus to the marks. Every section is worth 25 marks, so no single section can carry you. List the topics above and rate each one as strong, average or weak.
  2. Fix English and Reasoning fundamentals first. Grammar rules, vocabulary and the common reasoning formats (series, syllogism, coding-decoding, seating) reward clear basics more than shortcuts.
  3. Practise the calculation-heavy topics daily. Percentages, interest, time and work, and data interpretation take the most time in the paper, so short daily drills build speed.
  4. Give financial awareness a fixed slot. It is a full 25-mark section. Read banking and financial news regularly instead of cramming it at the end.
  5. Take timed mocks. Practise finishing 100 questions in 60 minutes, about 36 seconds per question on average, and note which section eats the most time.
  6. Keep a revision sheet. Note formulas, idioms, vocabulary and the mistakes you repeat in mocks, and revisit them weekly.

Bank of Baroda Wealth Executive & Credit Analyst Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for both posts is assessed as on the cut-off date, 01.09.2026. Candidates must fulfil the mandatory qualification, experience, and age criteria specified below for the post they are applying for.

Educational Qualification

Post Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Wealth Executive Graduation in any discipline AND any one valid certification among: IC 38 (Insurance Institute of India), NISM Series V A (Mutual Fund Distributors), NISM Series XXI-A (PMS Distributors), or NISM Series V-D (Mutual Fund – Specialised Investment Fund Distributors). Preferred: 2-year full-time PG degree/diploma in Management or MBA (Finance/Marketing/Banking). Minimum 2 years of experience in sales of wealth products with leading public/private/foreign banks, broking, securities firms, asset management companies, or wealth management companies in India.
Credit Analyst – C&IC Graduation in any discipline AND Chartered Accountant. Mandatory: minimum 1 year of banking experience in a Scheduled Commercial Bank. Preferred: experience in Corporate Credit.

Note: Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organisation as on 01.09.2026 will not be considered for eligibility, except when it is part of current employment. Experience in clerical cadre is not considered for determining eligibility. The selection process may comprise Application Scrutiny, an Online Test, Psychometric Test, Group Discussion (GD) and/or Personal Interview (PI), or any other test deemed suitable by the Bank.

  • The minimum qualifying marks/percentage for Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for General & EWS category and 55% for other Reserved categories; the Bank reserves the right to change this at its discretion.
  • Candidates not clearing the PI will not be considered for final selection.
  • A Psychometric Test and/or PI assesses personality, communication, problem-solving, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country.
  • The Bank's shortlisting criteria are internal and confidential and are not shared with candidates.

Probation Period & Service Bond

  • Selected candidates will be on probation for a period of 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • JMG/S-I officers: must serve a minimum of 3 years, or pay an amount equal to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 2 lakh) if they leave before completing 3 years.
  • MMG/S-II officers: must serve a minimum of 3 years, or pay an amount equal to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 3 lakh) if they leave before completing 3 years.

  • Relevant documents supporting declared work experience (appointment letter, salary slip, relieving letter, experience certificate)

  3. Fill in the online application with accurate personal, educational, and category details. No change is permitted after clicking Submit.

Post Qualification Experience
Faculty Shall be a Graduate (any i.e., Science/Commerce/Arts) /Post-Graduate; preference may be given to MSW/MA in Rural Development/MA in Sociology/ Psychology/ B.Sc. (Veterinary), B.Sc. (Horticulture), B.Sc. (Agri.), B.Sc.( Agri. Marketing}/B.A. with B.Ed. etc. Previous experience as Faculty preferred.

Additional requirements for the Faculty post include:

  • Shall have a flair for teaching and possess sound Computer Knowledge.
  • Excellent communication skills in the local language essential, fluency in English and Hindi will be an added advantage.
  • Skills in Typing in Local Language essential.

Pay and Terms

The selected candidate will receive a consolidated salary of Rs. 30,000 - 2000x5 - Rs. 40,000/- per month. An annual performance incentive of Rs. 2,000/- every year will be based on a satisfactory review and performance of services rendered.

Additional allowances and terms include:

  • Fixed Conveyance Allowance [FCA]: Rs. 2,500/- per month on a declaration basis, subject to completion of a minimum number of visits for conducting EAPs, Follow ups, etc. Otherwise, the Director of the RSETIs shall consider paying proportionately.

Bank of Baroda Faculty Job Description

The support staff for Faculty at RSETIs shall perform the following duties and responsibilities:

  • Any other work assigned by the Director from time to time.
  • Work as Faculty of the Institute handling sessions relating to entrepreneurship, motivation personality development, business management, conducting business games etc., guiding/educating the trainees and coordinating the programmes of the Institute.
  • Conducting pre-training activities - EAPs, generation of applications and selection of candidates.
  • Assisting the Director in designing the Annual Action Plan and training programmes.
  • Arranging logistics for the training programmes, including training materials and arranging Guest faculty.
  • Providing post Training escort services including conducting follow-up meets/visits.
  • Providing counseling, credit linkage, preparation of project reports etc.
  • Preparation of Success Stories and circulation of a minimum of two stories per month to the Controlling Office/MoRD.
  • Preparation of Post Programme Report and monthly/periodical reports.
  • Assisting/Guiding the Office assistant in maintaining of Day book, General Ledger and all other registers and Books.
  • Design new training programs by collecting feedback on emerging business opportunities in the area.
  • Prepare case studies and training materials for effective delivery of sessions and establish liaison with outside agencies.
  • Assist Director in internal control/administration, organizing functions, events, and meetings of the Institute.
  • Preparation of Press release/reports on various activities, supervising assistant, attender, watchman cum Gardner, and monitoring Guest faculty performance.
  • Maintenance of Inventory and Library books, and overseeing the maintenance of the entire campus including classrooms, kitchen, dining, and dormitory to keep premises clean and tidy.
  • Maintaining discipline in the Institute and ensuring administration of MILLY, LOG, PRAYER, YOGA, SHRAMADHAN etc., on daily basis.

Eligibility Criteria and Age Limit

The age limit for the Faculty post is 22 to 40 years as on 01.10.2026.

Selection Process

  1. Written Test: To assess General Knowledge and Computer capability.
  2. Personal Interview: To assess communication ability, leadership qualities, attitude, problem-solving ability, ability to get along with the trainees, and developmental approach.
  3. Demonstration/Presentation: To assess teaching skills and communication capability.

Exim Bank Deputy Manager & Manager Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility (age, educational qualification, etc.) is computed as on 31-08-2026, as detailed below for each post.

Manager (Grade/Scale MM II) – Internal Audit (2 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA). The Post Graduation course should be a minimum 2-year full-time duration with a specialization in Finance and minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA. For CA, passing the professional examination is sufficient, and membership of ICAI is mandatory.

Experience: Minimum 3 years of experience in a scheduled commercial bank, an all-India financial institution, or another organization of repute, in internal audit / credit audit, including handling preparation and submission of reports by internal/concurrent auditors, audit compliance, analysis and timely submission of audit observations to the audit committee, review of internal/concurrent audit scope and systems/procedures/controls, and experience dealing with RBI on audit/inspection matters (in Scale I or equivalent).

Deputy Manager (Grade/Scale JM I) – Banking Operations (6 Posts)

Qualification: Minimum 50% aggregate marks / equivalent CGPA in Graduation (minimum 3-year full-time course), AND Post Graduation (MBA / PGDBA / PGDBM / MMS) with specialization in Finance / International Business / Foreign Trade, or Chartered Accountant (CA), on the same terms as above.

A pre-recruitment training will be organised for candidates from reserved categories who opt for it through the online application form.

How to Apply for Exim Bank Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply online only, from 15 September 2026 to 21 October 2026. No other mode of application will be accepted.

  3. Fill in the application form; use "SAVE AND NEXT" to save progress before final submission, since no changes are possible after clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION."
  4. Upload your Photograph, Signature, Left Thumb Impression, and Handwritten Declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  5. Fill in remaining details, preview the application, and click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" only after verifying all details.
  6. Proceed to the "Payment" tab and complete the online fee payment, then click "Submit."
  7. Take a printout of the e-Receipt and the completed online application form for future reference.

Note: Candidates can apply for only one post. If a candidate applies for more than one post, only the latest valid (completed) application/registration will be retained, and fees paid for other registrations will stand forfeited.

  • Deputy Managers must execute a personal bond of ₹3 lakhs to serve the Bank for a minimum of 5 years from the date of joining.

  • Selected candidates already in service must produce a proper relieving letter/discharge certificate in original at the time of joining.
  • Any legal proceedings related to this advertisement can be instituted only in Mumbai, with courts/tribunals in Mumbai having sole and exclusive jurisdiction.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel, restrict, curtail, or enlarge the recruitment process, including the number of vacancies, at any stage without notice.
  • Candidates whose writing speed is permanently affected may use a scribe at their own cost and arrangement, subject to the Bank's stipulated scribe guidelines, and will be eligible for compensatory time of 20 minutes per hour of examination if registered for it in advance.

Action against misconduct: Candidates found using unfair means, impersonation, misbehaviour in the examination/interview hall, disclosing or transmitting exam content, carrying mobile phones/electronic devices into the hall, or providing false information may be disqualified from the examination, debarred from future Bank examinations, or, if already employed, have their service terminated - in addition to being liable for criminal prosecution.

SBI Specialist Cadre Officer Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfil the eligibility criteria for the post as on the date of eligibility, which is 31.08.2026 for educational qualification, experience and age. The educational qualification prescribed is the minimum, and candidates must possess the qualification and relevant full-time experience as on the specified dates. Meeting the minimum criteria does not entitle a candidate to be called for interview.

Key Eligibility Conditions

  • Only Indian citizens can apply.
  • Teaching and training experience will not be counted for eligibility.
  • Experience of less than six months in any organization will not be considered for eligibility.
  • The employer's experience certificate must specifically state that the candidate has experience in the related field as required.
  • Candidates can apply for more than one post if they fulfil all eligibility criteria for each post.
  • Candidates working in SBI Group companies must produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from their employer while applying.
  • Candidates with adverse reports regarding character and antecedents, moral turpitude, etc. are not eligible to apply.
  • Candidates selected and issued offer letters in previous Wealth Management & Premier Banking (WBPM) recruitment who did not join are debarred from applying for two (2) years from the date of non-joining.
  • Candidates previously engaged on contract for the posts in this advertisement who resigned are debarred from applying for any post in this advertisement for two (2) years from the date of resignation. Where a caution notice has been issued, such candidates are barred from appearing in all forthcoming recruitments.

  • Should have managed a large team of relationship managers and Team Leads at a national level.

  • Excellent knowledge of local and global economic trends.
  • Excellent knowledge of local Primary/Secondary Equity Markets/Fixed Income and of PMS/AIF/MF/Structured Products schemes in India.
  • Experience in creating views and research-based publications on capital market / sector trends.
  • Proficiency in using Excel / Modeling techniques / Bloomberg / Reuters / Morning Star / CRISIL databases.

Work experience is reckoned from the details in the Biodata/Resume at the time of shortlisting and interview. Verification is carried out at the time of interview or joining through one or more of these documents:

  • Annual performance appraisal letters; and/or
  • Combination of appointment and relieving letters; and/or
  • Combination of offer letter and IT returns; and/or
  • Any other authentic documentary evidence substantiating the period of experience, subject to satisfactory background and reference checks.

The application fee and intimation charges (non-refundable) are ₹750/- (Seven Hundred Fifty only) for UR/EWS/OBC candidates. There are no fees or intimation charges for SC/ST/PwBD candidates.

  • In case of multiple applications, only the last valid (completed) application is retained, and the fee paid for other registrations is forfeited.

SBI Specialist Cadre Officer Salary (CTC) and Contract Period

SBI has specified an annual CTC upper limit for each post. The annual CTC is negotiable and depends on the candidate's experience, current emoluments in present employment and place of posting. The CTC upper range covers Fixed Pay plus Variable Pay/PLP (based on Performance Rating) plus other perks. The notification does not give a monthly salary figure.

Contract Period, Leave and Notice Period

  • Variable pay: Officers are eligible for Performance Linked Pay and Annual Increment based on the performance rating measured as per the Bank's Policy.
  • Contract period: 5 years, renewable for another 4 years at the discretion of the Bank, subject to fulfilment of any conditions the Bank may stipulate.
  • Leave: Officers engaged on contract (OECs) are entitled to 30 days of leave during the financial year, granted by the Bank for genuine and appropriate reasons.
  • Notice period: The contract can be terminated at any time, without assigning any reason, by giving 2 months' notice from either side or by payment/surrender of 2 months' compensation in lieu.
  • Transfer policy: The Bank may transfer OECs to any SBI office in India or depute them to associates, subsidiaries or other organizations. Requests for posting or transfer to a specific place or office may not be entertained.

SBI Specialist Cadre Officer Selection Process

The selection process comprises shortlisting of candidates, followed by one or more rounds of personal/video interview and CTC negotiation. There is no written test mentioned in the notification.

  1. Shortlisting: A shortlisting committee constituted by the Bank decides the shortlisting parameters and the number of candidates to be called. Meeting the minimum qualification and experience does not give any right to be called for interview. The Bank's decision is final and no correspondence will be entertained. Shortlisting is provisional and without verification of original documents.
  2. Interview: The interview carries 100 marks. Qualifying marks will be decided by the Bank.
  3. CTC negotiation: The Bank may negotiate the CTC with shortlisted/provisionally qualified candidates either (a) at the time of the interview, individually, or (b) subsequent to the interview, on the same day after the interview process or on a later date. If negotiation is conducted separately, candidates are called in order of merit. A provisionally selected candidate who does not agree to the CTC offered is treated as having voluntarily exited the recruitment process, and the next candidate in merit may be considered.
  4. Merit list: Prepared in descending order of interview scores only. Candidates with the same cut-off marks are ranked by age in descending order.

The interview call letter or intimation will be sent by email or uploaded on the Bank's website. No hard copy will be sent. At the time of interview, original documents are verified, and candidates must provide details of any pending criminal cases. The Bank may also conduct independent verification, including police records.

How to Apply for SBI Specialist Cadre Officer Recruitment 2026

Candidates must apply online only. Hard copies of the application and other documents need not be sent to the Bank.

  1. Visit the official SBI careers page: https://sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings.
  2. Scroll down and click on the respective advertisement.
  3. Download Advertisement No. CRPD/SCO/2026-27/25 and read the detailed advertisement carefully.
  4. Click Apply Online and register. Keep a valid email ID active until the declaration of result.
  5. Fill in the application carefully. If you cannot complete it in one go, you can save it; a provisional registration number and password are generated. The saved application can be edited three times only.
  6. Upload the required photograph, signature and documents.
  7. Review the application before final submission. Corrections are not allowed after final submission.
  8. Pay the application fee online (if applicable) and take a printout of the e-receipt and application form.

Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to avoid website load or connectivity issues. SBI does not take responsibility for candidates unable to submit applications by the last date for such reasons.

  • Educational certificates: relevant mark-sheets/degree certificate (PDF)
  • Experience certificates (PDF)
  • Form-16/Offer Letter/Latest salary slip from current employer (PDF)
  • No Objection Certificate, if applicable (PDF)

How to Check Your RRC Prayagraj Group D DV Date and Shift

  1. Open the official DV schedule and cut-off PDF from the link in the Important Links section.
  2. Search for your 16-digit roll number using Ctrl+F on a computer or "Find in page" on a phone.
  3. Note the date and shift listed against your roll number.
  4. Download your E-call letter from www.rrcpryj.org when the link goes live, 5 to 7 days before your DV date.
  5. Print the E-call letter and read all instructions in it.

RRC Prayagraj Group D E-Call Letter

  • The download link will be active on www.rrcpryj.org 5 to 7 days before the DV date.
  • The E-call letter has blank spaces for the self-declaration paragraph, signature and left thumb impression (LTI). Leave them empty and fill them in only at the DV centre in front of the supervisor.
  • Candidates who write the declaration in capital or disjointed letters, or who sign or fill it in beforehand, may have their candidature cancelled.
  • No call letter will be sent by post. Information may also be sent by email and SMS.

Documents Required for RRC Prayagraj Group D Document Verification

Bring the original documents plus two sets of self-attested photocopies in A-4 size.

  1. Printout of the CBT E-call letter (candidate's copy) and the PET E-call letter, where applicable.
  2. One original valid photo ID along with the E-call letter. Accepted IDs: Voter ID, Aadhaar Card, printout of e-Aadhaar, Driving Licence, PAN Card, Passport, or a valid ID issued by the employer for government employees. Candidates without a photo ID will not be allowed to appear.
  3. Community certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS). OBC and EWS certificates must be valid on the date of the online application and also currently valid.
  4. Disability certificate and UDID card for candidates with disabilities.
  5. All mark sheets and certificates for educational and technical qualifications.
  6. Twelve coloured passport-size photographs, matching the photo uploaded in the online application.
  7. An affidavit, as per the CEN 08/2024 instructions, if there is any spelling difference in your name or in your parents' names across documents.
  8. Class 10 pass certificate, or ITI / equivalent, or National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC) from NCVT.
  9. No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the employer for candidates already in service (central or state government, Railways or PSUs, including those on probation or training).
  10. Income certificate (Annexure III-A) for EBC candidates, and a declaration as per Annexure IV for minority candidates claiming the examination fee concession.
  11. Any other certificate or document that is required.

RRC Prayagraj Group D Medical Examination

  • Candidates who clear DV will be sent for the medical examination on the next working day.
  • The medical is held at a designated Railway hospital under North Central Railway: the Divisional Hospital at Prayagraj, Kanpur, Agra or Jhansi.
  • Be prepared to stay for at least 4 days at your own cost.
  • The medical examination fee is Rs. 24, and no other fee is charged.
  • In rare cases where a test such as a CT scan, ultrasound or eye surgery evaluation is needed and not available in the Railway hospital, the candidate must pay the outside laboratory or hospital charges.
  • Carry a valid and current photo ID for the medical.

Important Instructions for Shortlisted Candidates

  • Shortlisting is not final. Eligibility will be decided only on the basis of the online application details and verification of original documents.
  • If any information is found false or hidden, or if you do not meet the qualification, age, category or medical standards, your candidature will be cancelled and you may be barred from Railway or other government recruitment exams.
  • Being called for DV or receiving an E-call letter does not give any right to a job.
  • The date of birth must match your Class 10 or equivalent certificate. No request to change the date of birth will be accepted, and any mismatch leads to disqualification.
  • Reservation benefits (SC, ST, OBC-NCL, EWS) need original certificates in the prescribed format: Annexure-I for SC/ST, Annexure-II for OBC-NCL and Annexure-III for EWS.
  • Requests to change the DV centre, date or shift will not be accepted. If you do not appear for DV, your candidature will be cancelled.
  • Biometric details will be taken at every stage. Any discrepancy can lead to disqualification and legal action.
  • Using unfair means or impersonation can lead to a lifetime bar from all RRB/RRC exams and from Railway employment, and service may be terminated if already appointed.
  • RRC may conduct additional DV, cancel or modify the recruitment process at any stage, and correct typing or printing errors. The decision of RRC is final.
  • Check www.rrcpryj.org regularly for updates.

What Is the RBI Assistant Language Proficiency Test?

The RBI Assistant Language Proficiency Test checks whether a shortlisted candidate can read, write, understand and speak the official or local language of the recruitment office they applied to. The LPT is separate from the Preliminary and Main examinations.

  • The LPT is meant for candidates provisionally shortlisted on the basis of their Main Examination performance.
  • Clearing the written examinations does not complete the selection process. The language requirement must also be fulfilled.

Assam Rifles Technical/ Tradesman Recruitment 2026 : Educational Qualification

Post Name Eligibility 
Warrant Officer (Cipher)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 12th in Science with Physics, Mathematics, and English, along with a 2-year ITI course (NSQF Level 4 or above) in ICT, IT, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Instrumentation Technology.
Rifleman (Lineman Field)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Electronics Engineering, Electronics Mechanic, Electrical Engineering, Electrician Power Distribution, Electrician, Instrumentation Technology, Instrument Mechanic, Technician Power Electronic System, Technician Electronic System Design & Repair, Fibre to Home Technician, or OFC Technician.
Rifleman (Engineer Equipment Mechanic)
  • Candidates msut have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI in Power Electric Systems Mechanic or Mechanic Diesel. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Engineering Equipment Mechanic from a recognized institution.
Rifleman (Electrician Motor Vehicle)
  • Candidates msut have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Electrician, Electrical Engineering, Technical, Power Electronics, or Communication System from a recognized institution.
Rifleman (Metalsmith)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Metalsmith or Metallurgy from a recognized institution.
Rifleman Store Keeper Technical (EME)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th from a recognized board or institution.
Rifleman (Welder)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a Diploma in Welder or Metallurgy from a recognized institution.
Warrant Officer (Operation Theatre Technician)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 12th and hold a minimum 2-year Diploma in Operation Theatre Technician.
Rifleman (Mason)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th, qualify the required Trade Test, and provide a self-certification/undertaking confirming at least 1 year of work experience in the relevant trade.
Rifleman (Electrical Fitter Signal)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Electrical Engineering, Electrician Power Distribution, Electrician, Instrumentation Technology, Instrument Mechanic, Technician Power Electronic System, or Technician Electronic System Design & Repair.
Rifleman (Armorer)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th and hold an ITI certificate in the Welding trade from a recognized institution.
Rifleman (Recovery Vehicle Mechanic)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th and hold a 2-year ITI certificate in Recovery Vehicle Mechanic, along with a valid Heavy Motor Vehicle (HMV)/Transport Vehicle Driving License. Alternatively, candidates with Class 10th pass and a valid HMV/Transport Vehicle Driving License are also eligible.
Havildar (Instrument Mechanic)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Instrument Mechanic, Instrument Technology, Electronic Mechanic, or Electronic Technology from a recognized institution.
Rifleman (Upholster)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Upholstery/Upholster Trade from a recognized institution.
Rifleman (Vehicle Mechanic)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th with a minimum 2 years of technical training from ITI. Alternatively, candidates can have a 2 or 3-year Diploma in Mechanic Motor Vehicle, Mechanic, Mechanic Diesel, Fitter, Mechanic Engineering Technology, or Automobile Engineering from a recognized institution.
Warrant Officer (Draughtsman)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 10th and hold a 3-year Diploma in Architectural Assistantship from any recognized Polytechnic College or Institution.
Warrant Officer (Physiotherapist)
  • Candidates must have passed Class 12th and hold a minimum 2-year Diploma in Physiotherapy. They must also have at least 1 year of work experience as a Physiotherapist in a recognized hospital or physiotherapy centre with a minimum capacity of 50 beds.

How to Check the JKSSB Junior Laboratory Technician Provisional Answer Key 2026

The Provisional Answer Key is part of the official notice PDF published on the JKSSB website. Annexure "A" lists the answers for all 120 questions across the four series.

  1. Open the official notice PDF using the link in the Important Links section below.
  2. Go to Annexure "A", titled Provisional Answer Key of the Written Examination for the post of Junior Laboratory Technician conducted on 14/10/2026.
  3. Check the series (A, B, C or D) of your question booklet.
  4. Find the column for your series and compare the option for each question number with the answer you marked on your OMR sheet.
  5. Note any answer you believe is wrong and keep supporting proof ready before you decide to object.

JKSSB Junior Laboratory Technician Answer Key Objection Process

JKSSB accepts objections only in offline mode. Online and any other mode of submission will not be entertained, and the Board will not entertain objections after the stipulated period.

  1. Download and fill the prescribed Annexure "B" proforma attached to the notice.
  2. Use a separate form for each question, and put each question on a separate page. If several questions are entered in one form, only the first question will be considered.
  3. Attach documentary proof or evidence supporting your claim (hard copies only).
  4. Prepare a demand draft of Rs. 200 per question in favour of the Accounts Officer, J&K Services Selection Board.
  5. Submit the hard copies in person at the JKSSB office, Muthi, Akhnoor Road, Jammu, or at JKSSB, Zamzam Building, Rambagh, Srinagar, between 11:00 AM and 05:00 PM on the permitted working days.

The Annexure "B" proforma asks for the following information. Fill every field legibly and sign the form.

  • Date of exam
  • Exam centre division (Jammu/Kashmir)
  • Correspondence address and contact/mobile number
  • Demand draft number and date
  • Candidate's 16-digit account number and IFSC code
  • Question number and series
  • Details of the objection
  • Resource material (a copy must be enclosed)
  • Correct answer/option as per the candidate
  • Remarks, date of application and signature of the candidate

Can Candidates Raise Objections to Kerala PSC University Assistant Provisional Answer Key 2026?

What Is the Difference Between Provisional and Final Answer Key?

A provisional answer key is the initial official set of answers published after an examination. A final answer key may be issued after the commission reviews valid objections and makes any necessary corrections.

How to Calculate Your KSET 2026 Score Using the Answer Key

Compare each response on your OMR sheet copy with the official key. Count the correct answers in Paper I and Paper II. Use this formula:

Total Score = (Correct answers in Paper I + Correct answers in Paper II) × 2

For example, a candidate with 30 correct answers in Paper I and 60 in Paper II has 90 correct answers in total. The estimated score is 90 × 2 = 180 out of 300. This example is for illustration only.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

  • Statistics Paper I - Covers topics such as Probability, Statistical Methods, Numerical Analysis, and related areas.
  • Statistics Paper II - Covers topics including Linear Models, Statistical Inference, Sampling Theory, and Econometrics.

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

UPSC allows candidates to challenge answers in the provisional answer key by submitting a formal representation. The process for raising objections is as follows:

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

Things to Know About the Response Sheet

  • Personal use only. The saved question paper is meant for self-analysis, not for sharing.

How to Raise an Objection Against the SSC Selection Post Answer Key

If you believe an answer in the tentative key is wrong, you can challenge it online before 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM. Each challenged question costs ₹50.

  1. Log in to the SSC portal.
  2. Open the Challenge/Objection Management link for Phase-XIV/2026.
  3. Select the question or questions you want to challenge.
  4. Enter your suggested answer and upload supporting documents or a justification.
  5. Pay the ₹50 fee for each question challenged.
  6. Submit the objection before the deadline.

Rules to remember

  • Objections are accepted online only.
  • Objections received after 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM will not be entertained.
  • The final answer key is prepared after reviewing valid objections.
  • Candidates cannot challenge the final answer key.

How to Calculate Your Marks Using the Answer Key

Particulars Marks

Total marks 200
Correct answer +2
Wrong answer −0.50
Unattempted 0

Formula: Total marks = (Correct answers × 2) − (Wrong answers × 0.50)

Example: A candidate attempts 85 questions, with 70 correct and 15 wrong. Marks = (70 × 2) − (15 × 0.50) = 140 − 7.5 = 132.5.

This is only an estimate. The answer key is tentative, and your score may change if SSC revises any answer after reviewing objections.

What Happens After the SSC Selection Post Answer Key?

  • The objection window closes on 12 October 2026, 4:00 PM.
  • SSC reviews the valid objections.
  • The final answer key is released.
  • The result and category-wise cut-off marks follow.
  • Shortlisted candidates are called for Document Verification.

SSC CGL Tier 2 Final Answer Key 2026 - Download Link, Scorecard, and Marking Scheme

The Staff Selection Commission released the SSC CGL Tier 2 Final Answer Key 2026 on 17th June 2026, along with individual scorecards and response sheets for the Combined Graduate Level Examination 2025-26. Candidates who appeared in the Tier 2 exam, held on 18th and 19th January 2026, can now log in at ssc.gov.in using their Registration ID and password to download their final answer key, marks, and response sheet. The facility is available until 16th July 2026 (9:00 PM), after which the documents will no longer be accessible.

This release comes more than two months after SSC declared the Tier 2 final result on 8th April 2026, where 15,118 candidates were provisionally selected for various Group B and Group C posts. The final answer key now gives every candidate, selected or not, a way to verify exactly how their score was calculated.

Click Here: SSC CGL Tier 2 Final Answer Key 2026

What Is the SSC CGL Tier 2 Final Answer Key 2026

This section explains what the final answer key actually is and how it differs from the result already announced earlier this year. The final answer key is the Commission's conclusively reviewed set of correct answers for every question in the Tier 2 exam, finalized after evaluating all objections submitted against the provisional key.

Unlike the provisional answer key released on 30th January 2026, this final version cannot be challenged further. It is the key against which your actual Tier 2 marks were computed, and it is now being made available alongside your scorecard so you can independently verify your result. Since the final result and merit list were already published on 8th April 2026, this release functions primarily as a transparency and verification step rather than one that changes selection outcomes.
